A completed, print-ready PDF

An editable Canva copy for future updates

This service includes customization of my existing 24-page design, including replacing text, photos, property details, and adjusting colours.

This is a made-to-order digital product. No physical item will be shipped.

All photos and property information must be supplied by the buyer.

Your finished Welcome Book is intended for use at your own rental property and may not be resold or redistributed as a template.

• An editable Canva welcome-book template with 30 guest-information pages: 20 core pages plus 10 additional pages.
• A separate illustration library page containing 15 additional images to swap into your book.
• A PDF containing the Canva template link and practical editing instructions.

01. Cover — add your property name.
02. Welcome & essentials — Wi-Fi, address, host contact and checkout details.
03. Your guide — contents and an overview of the book.
04. Arrival & access — check-in, directions, keys and entrance/access photos.

07. Safety & emergencies — property address, emergency contacts, safety equipment and exit information.

18. FAQs & troubleshooting — answers to common guest questions.
19. Before you go — checkout tasks, key return and locking up.

results.title: Airbnb Welcome Book Printable, Guest House Manual for Vacation Rental Hosts, Wifi, House Rules and Local Guide, 12 Page PDF
results.description:
Guests ask the same eight questions. Where do I park, how does the heat work, when is bin day, what is there to eat near here. This is where you answer them once, in your own handwriting, and leave it where they will actually find it.

Twelve pages. You fill in the first two as the host, and pages three to twelve are the book your guests read.

WHAT'S INSIDE
• Start here, for the host, and a forty minute order to fill it in
• Before your first guest: what to print, what to stock, and what to reprint later
• Welcome: the note from you, wifi, check out time, and the people nearby
• Arriving and leaving: parking, the door, finding the place, and what to do before they go
• How the house works: heat, hot water, kitchen, laundry, TV, and well or tank water
• House rules, plainly, with the usual questions answered in a line each
• Bins, recycling, and the short list for before they leave
• If something goes wrong: shutoffs, the five problems that actually happen, and who to call
• Where we eat: your three, then everything else
• What to do nearby, within ten minutes and worth the drive
• The place by season, because guests arrive in February too
• Thank you, a guest book, and a page for what you changed

WHY THIS ONE IS SHORT
Most welcome books are thirty pages and read like a lease. Guests skim five. This one keeps the answers on the pages they'll reach for, in plain sentences, and the handwriting reads as a person rather than a policy.

ONE HABIT THROUGHOUT
Door codes and alarm codes go on the printed copy that stays inside the house, never in a listing, a photo, or a message thread. The book says so on the page where you'd be tempted.

WHAT IT WON'T DO
It explains how the house works. It is not a rental agreement, and nothing in it is legal or insurance advice. It is also not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to any booking platform.

PRINT IT OR FILL IT IN
A regular PDF with no fill-in form fields. Print at actual size, or type onto it with the free Fill & Sign tool in Adobe Acrobat Reader, the markup tools on an iPhone or iPad, or Preview on a Mac.

Shopping on your phone? Etsy's app can't download digital files yet. Open Etsy in your phone's web browser instead, sign in, and download from your Purchases page.

GOES WELL WITH
The Household Emergency Binder for the shutoffs and the call list, and The Sitter Sheet if someone looks after the place while you're away.

WHAT YOU GET
One PDF, 12 pages, US Letter. Instant download, nothing ships.

Warm off-white, charcoal and one deep green. It suits a city apartment, a cabin, or a family beach house.

results.description:
Instant WiFi access for your guests - one tap or scan and they're connected. No app, no typing, no hassle.

This handcrafted Baltic birch sign is laser-engraved with your property name and WiFi details, plus a pre-programmed NFC chip. Tap or scan -  both included, both ready to use.

★ WHY OURS
 Most WiFi signs only give a QR code. Ours adds NFC tap too, so it works on every phone - and your name (plus logo, if you'd like) makes it feel like part of the space, not an afterthought.

★ 2 SIZES & DIMENSIONS
🔹 SMALL — 9 × 12 cm 
Perfect for: Reception desks · Individual offices · Meeting room tables · Consultation rooms · Any space where one client is seen at a time

🔹 LARGE — 12 × 17 cm 
Perfect for: Office lobbies · Front desk counters · High-traffic entrances · Waiting areas · Any space that needs to be visible from across the room

Base: 9mm thick wooden stand, included

★ HOW TO ORDER
Just a few quick things we need from you:

1. Your property or business name
Type it into the Personalization box at checkout — this is what will be engraved at the top of the sign.

2. Your WiFi network name and password
Type the exact network name (SSID) and password into the Personalization box, spelled and cased exactly as they should appear - for example: "Network: OliveGuest / Password: welcomehome." Double-check this before submitting, since it's exactly what we'll engrave.

Please include:

WiFi Network Name (SSID)
Password
Security type (WPA2 / WPA3 / WEP / Open)
Hidden network? (Yes / No)

3. Your logo -  only if you've added the logo upgrade
Attach a high-resolution file (PNG, SVG, or JPG works best) as a photo in the Personalization box.

Before we cut anything, we double-check your name, WiFi details, and logo with you. If you'd like to see a preview before we go into production, just send us a message.

★ WHAT'S INCLUDED 
✔ Laser-engraved Baltic birch sign, standard size 
✔ Your property/business name, engraved 
✔ Your WiFi network & password, engraved 
✔ 9mm Baltic birch base, no tools needed

✔ Static QR code, laser-engraved — never fades 
✔ "TAP OR SCAN – to connect," engraved 
✔ Optional: your logo, engraved alongside your name

★ PLEASE NOTE ABOUT NFC & iPHONE

NFC WiFi functionality is different between iPhone and Android.

Android: Compatible devices can connect to WiFi automatically through NFC.

iPhone: iOS does not allow an NFC WiFi tag to directly join the network in the same way. Instead, our NFC tag opens a webpage containing your WiFi information, allowing guests to easily copy the password and paste it into their WiFi settings.

For iPhone users, we recommend using the QR code for the fastest connection.

The NFC feature is still fully functional on iPhone - it simply provides access to the WiFi information rather than automatically joining the network.

★ WHY BALTIC BIRCH 
Warmer and more premium than acrylic or plastic - real texture, real grain, no two signs alike.

results.title: Airbnb Guest Cards Template | Editable Canva Signs | WiFi, House Rules, Check-Out & More
results.description:
Your guests need information. Your walls don't need instructions.
The Guest Cards Collection turns Wi-Fi details, house guidelines, check-out information and everyday guest questions into beautifully written, editable Canva cards designed to belong in a considered Airbnb or short-term rental.

THE GUEST CARDS COLLECTION
Practical information, without turning your home into a rulebook.

Every host needs to communicate.
The Wi-Fi password.
Where to park.
What time quiet hours begin.
Where the extra towels are.
How check-out works.

But there is a difference between giving guests information and covering a beautiful rental in signs.
The Guest Cards Collection was created for hosts who want both.
Clear guidance for the guest.
A considered interior for everyone else.
A collection of beautifully designed, thoughtfully written guest cards that help practical information feel like part of the hospitality — not an interruption to it.
Gentle in tone. Clear in purpose.

YOUR HOUSE RULES SHOULDN'T FEEL LIKE RULES.
There is a reason handwritten notes, laminated warnings and giant "DO NOT" signs feel wrong inside an otherwise beautiful property.
They change the atmosphere.
Suddenly the guest is no longer being welcomed.
They are being managed.
The Guest Cards Collection takes the same practical information and gives it a different voice:
warm, concise, clear and human.
Instead of:
NO SHOES.
you can say:
"The floors are clean and the slippers are warm — both are for you. Leave your shoes by the door; your feet are off duty now."
Instead of a cold NO SMOKING sign:
"We keep the air linen-fresh for every guest who sleeps here. If you smoke — the balcony has the better view anyway."
The message still lands.
It just sounds like hospitality.

NOT SIGNS. PART OF THE STAY.
These cards are designed to do three things at once:
GUIDE — Put useful information exactly where the guest needs it.
WELCOME — Use language that feels warm rather than corrective.
BELONG — Make the card feel considered enough to live inside a styled interior.
That means the Wi-Fi information can sit beautifully on a shelf.
The Coffee Ritual can live beside the coffee machine.
The Sleep Menu can sit on a bedside table.
And the Check-Out card can appear by the door when it is actually relevant.
The information becomes part of the experience instead of visual clutter.

ONE COLLECTION. FOUR LAYOUTS.
22 signature cards come in four coordinated layouts each:
Band · Header · Full · Frame
Choose the layout that suits your space, then keep the same format throughout the property for a polished, consistent look. The files are designed to be personalised, then printed at A5 or framed at A4 depending on placement.
You get options because every interior is different.
But the system is deliberately built around consistency, not mixing everything together.

FOUR REFINED COLOURWAYS
Choose the palette that belongs in your property:
COFFEE — deep, warm and quietly sophisticated
MOSS — soft, natural and understated
OLIVE — earthy, elegant and calm
TERRACOTTA — warm, sun-washed and welcoming
The included Placement Guide specifically recommends choosing one colourway and one layout for the whole home so the result feels intentional rather than pieced together.

CARDS FOR THE QUESTIONS GUESTS ACTUALLY HAVE
The collection covers practical information throughout the stay:
Welcome Home · Wi-Fi · Check-Out · House Guidelines · Important Contacts · Waste & Recycling · Parking · Shoes Off, Slippers On · Quiet Hours · A Smoke-Free Home · Your Towels · The Guest Pantry · The Bed Is Yours · If Something's Not Right · The First Evening · The Coffee Ritual · Golden Hour · The Sleep Menu · A Rainy Day · The Story of This Place · Share the Love · The Digital Guidebook (QR)
Plus: Getting In (lockbox), 4 appliance cards (Washing Machine, Heating & Cooling, TV & Streaming, Coffee Maker) and 2 team cards for your cleaners (Cleaning Standard, Restock List).
29 cards in total.
The important thing is that these are not generic labels.
They are already thoughtfully written, with dotted fields for your own details — so you are editing useful hospitality copy rather than staring at another blank Canva template.

THE DIFFERENCE IS IN THE WRITING.
A guest card should answer the question quickly.
But the way it answers matters.
Compare:
QUIET HOURS: 10 PM–7 AM.
with:
"Sleep is the best amenity we offer. Help us protect it — for you, and for the neighbours who live here all year."
Same information.
Completely different feeling.
Or a standard towel note versus:
"The dark one? Make-up friendly. Use it guilt-free."
It solves a practical problem while still sounding like someone thought about the guest.
That is the idea behind the whole collection.
Information can be clear without being cold.

SOME CARDS GUIDE. OTHERS CREATE A MOMENT.
Not every card exists because a guest has a problem.
Some exist because good hospitality notices opportunities.
THE COFFEE RITUAL — Tell guests where the coffee is — and point them toward the best seat in the house for a slow morning.
GOLDEN HOUR — Tell them when and where the light in your property turns beautiful.
THE SLEEP MENU — Show them the pillow options, blackout setup, lighter duvet or white noise.
A RAINY DAY — Give them a Plan B before bad weather becomes disappointment.
These are small additions.
But they can change the property from somewhere to sleep into somewhere that feels hosted.

AND YES — THERE IS A RIGHT WAY TO USE THEM.
This collection includes what may be its most important part:
THE PLACEMENT GUIDE
Because giving you beautiful cards and then encouraging you to put twenty of them on the walls would defeat the entire point.
The core rule is simple:
ONE VISIBLE CARD PER ROOM. MAXIMUM.
Everything else belongs:
in the Welcome Book,
inside a useful drawer,
or directly beside the thing it explains.
The guide tells you exactly where different cards belong — from the entryway and kitchen to the bedroom, bathroom and check-out area.
This is what makes the collection feel much more like a designed hospitality system than a bundle of printable signs.

FROM "SIGN" TO STYLING OBJECT.
The Placement Guide also covers:
recommended print sizes · paper finish · frame profiles · frame materials · hanging height · standing vs. hanging placement · visual consistency
For example, it recommends A5 for shelves and consoles, A4 primarily for the entry welcome card, matte 200–250 gsm paper, thin frames coordinated with the property's existing finishes, and a gallery-standard 152 cm centre height for hung cards.
Because there is a huge visual difference between:
a sign someone printed
and
a small object that looks like it belongs in the room.

THE BOUTIQUE-HOTEL TEST.
Before a card goes anywhere, the included final check asks five questions, including:
Is there already another visible card in this room?
Is it within arm's reach of the thing it explains?
Would a boutique hotel display this — or hide it in a drawer?
Does the frame belong with the finishes in the room?
Would this card make a photograph of the corner better or worse?
That one little test says a lot about what this collection is trying to do.
Inform the guest without compromising the interior.

EDIT. PRINT. PLACE. DONE.
The process is intentionally simple.
01 · CHOOSE YOUR COLOURWAY — Coffee, Moss, Olive or Terracotta.
02 · CHOOSE YOUR LAYOUT — Band, Header, Full or Frame — and keep it consistent.
03 · MAKE IT YOURS — Replace the editable details with your own Wi-Fi, parking, check-out times, contact information and recommendations.
04 · PRINT OR FRAME — Use the included guidance to choose the right size and finish.
05 · PLACE WITH INTENTION — Follow the Placement Guide so every card earns its spot.
Then stop.
No wall of instructions required.

WHAT YOU RECEIVE

✦ 29 cards — 22 of them in four layouts: Band · Header · Full · Frame
✦ Print at A5 or frame at A4
✦ The Placement Guide — print-ready PDF in A4 and US Letter (4 pages)
✦ Professionally written hospitality copy
✦ Wi-Fi card
✦ Welcome card
✦ Check-out card
✦ House Guidelines
✦ Important Contacts
✦ Parking information
✦ Waste & Recycling
✦ Quiet Hours
✦ Smoke-Free Home
✦ Towels & bathroom guidance
✦ Guest Pantry
✦ Bedroom & sleep guidance
✦ Coffee Ritual
✦ First Evening recommendations
✦ Golden Hour
✦ Rainy Day ideas
✦ Review / QR card
✦ Digital Guidebook QR card
✦ Getting In (lockbox) card
✦ 4 appliance cards
✦ 2 team cards for your cleaners
✦ Printing, framing & styling guidance
Digital product — no physical item or frame will be shipped.

PERFECT FOR
— Airbnb hosts
— Vacation rental owners
— Short-term rental hosts
— VRBO properties

— Guest houses
— Property managers
— Interior-conscious hosts
— Hosts who want clearer guest communication without covering their property in instructions

THIS COLLECTION IS FOR YOU IF…
— you keep leaving handwritten notes around the property.
— your guests repeatedly ask where something is.
— you need house rules but hate the way "house rules signs" look.
— you want your Wi-Fi information accessible without sticking a password to the fridge.
— you want practical communication to feel consistent with the rest of your interior.
— you care just as much about how something is said as what it says.
And especially if you have ever thought:
"I need guests to know this. I just don't want an ugly sign saying it."
That is exactly what these cards were created for.

CLEAR ENOUGH TO GUIDE.
BEAUTIFUL ENOUGH TO BELONG.
The best guest communication does not shout.

WHERE CAN I FIND MORE ANSWERS AND TUTORIALS?
Visit my FAQ Help Center, where I've gathered answers to the most common questions, with step-by-step guides:
👉 sites.google.com/view/templates4brandinghelpcenter/home
If you don't find your answer, message me on Etsy. I'll be happy to help 😊

DO I NEED CANVA PRO TO EDIT MY INVITATION?
No! All my templates work with a free Canva account. You can edit on a computer, phone or tablet.

HOW DO I DOWNLOAD MY TEMPLATE?
After purchase, log into Etsy from a web browser (the download button doesn't appear in the Etsy app), go to "Your account" › "Purchases and reviews" and click "Download Files". Open the PDF and click the Canva link inside to start editing.

CAN I EDIT THE INVITATION IN SPANISH OR ANOTHER LANGUAGE?
Yes! Every word is editable, so you can write your invitation in English, Spanish or any language, or make it bilingual.

CAN YOU EDIT THE INVITATION FOR ME?
Of course! For small changes, just message me. For a done-for-you invitation, I offer a Full Editing Service (48h), available in my shop under "Add-Ons & Edits".

CAN YOU MAKE MY CUSTOM THEME OR CUSTOM COLORS INVITATION?
Please contact me before purchasing and send me your inspiration, color palette, and the template you would like me to customize. I’ll send you a first preview, and if you love it, you can then purchase the matching editing service from my shop under “Add-Ons & Edits.”

WHAT IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A VIDEO INVITATION AND A WEBSITE INVITATION?
Both options are digital and can be sent by email, text message, WhatsApp, or social media.

✔ A video invitation is an MP4 file with music, animations, photos, and a QR code for RSVP. The video and music play automatically when your guests open or play the file. It is beautiful and easy to share, but it does not include clickable buttons or interactive sections.

✔ A website invitation is a scrollable interactive Canva website link. It can include clickable RSVP, Google Maps, countdown, gift registry, schedule, photo gallery, FAQ, and other interactive features. Please note that music on a website invitation is click-to-play only and cannot autoplay.

HOW DO MY GUESTS RSVP?
It depends on your invitation type:

🌐 Website invitation: guests fill in the embedded form or tap the RSVP button right on your invitation.
🎬 Video invitation: guests scan the QR code in the video.

Either way, they RSVP in one click, with no app or account needed. You can choose the RSVP option you prefer:
✔ Google Form: see every response in real time and receive email notifications
✔ A Canva Form
✔ Your own RSVP link, such as Zola, The Knot, Joy or any wedding website you already use

Don't need an RSVP? No problem! Everything is fully editable, so you can easily delete the RSVP button, section or page from your template.

CAN I GET A REFUND OR EXCHANGE?
Returns aren't accepted for digital downloads. However, if you purchased the wrong color or design by mistake, just message me and I'll be happy to exchange it for the one you wanted. And if anything goes wrong with your file, I'll gladly help until everything works perfectly 😊

results.description:
Convierte a todo tu equipo en embajadores de hospitalidad 5 estrellas con un PDF de descarga instantánea y diseño impecable.

La mayoría de los anfitriones se obsesionan con el espacio: las sábanas, la iluminación, la estación de café perfectamente estilizada. Y eso importa. Pero los mejores anfitriones saben una verdad silenciosa: la *sensación* es lo que genera reseñas brillantes, reservas repetidas y la posibilidad de cobrar tarifas premium.

Este no es un libro de bienvenida genérico. Es una guía de entrenamiento en comunicación y comportamiento para ti, tu coanfitrión, tu equipo de limpieza y cualquiera que lleve tu marca. Les da a todos las palabras, acciones y mentalidad exactas para que cada huésped se sienta genuinamente bienvenido, profundamente valorado y completamente cuidado — desde el primer mensaje hasta la despedida final.

---

QUÉ INCLUYE EL PDF DE 25 PÁGINAS

📘 Los 4 Secretos de la Llegada Mágica
La secuencia exacta de los primeros 30 segundos que define el tono emocional de toda la estancia. Entrena a tu equipo para aplicar Sonrisa, Postura, Ver y Simple & Específico de forma natural.

🗣️ Guiones de Saludos y Despedidas
Plantillas listas para copiar en mensajes, llamadas y bienvenidas en persona. Cubre prellegada, durante la estancia, salida, huéspedes que regresan, llegadas tarde y agradecimientos post-reseña. Sin necesidad de improvisar.

🛡️ Método L.A.S.T. para Quejas
Un marco paso a paso para manejar problemas sin pánico: Escuchar, Disculparse, Solucionar, Agradecer. Convierte una situación de 3 estrellas en una recuperación de 5 que genera más lealtad que una estancia perfecta.

✅ La Hoja Azul: 10 Reglas de Comportamiento No Negociables
El código cultural esencial del equipo. Cubre uso del teléfono, límites con huéspedes, normas sobre olores y comida, orgullo por la propiedad y la ceremonia de cierre "últimos oídos afuera". Imprímela, fíjala y hazla tu estándar.

🗓️ Ritmo de Comunicación de 5 Mensajes
Una cronología completa de mensajes que encantan al huésped: reserva instantánea → 3 días antes → noche 1 → mañana de salida → post-reseña. Lista para copiar en tu sistema automatizado o enviar manualmente.

🎁 BONO: Frases para Crisis y Tarjeta de Referencia Rápida
Guiones de bolsillo para plagas, cortes de luz, errores de reserva, quejas por ruido y cierres de puerta. Además, una tarjeta resumen de una página para imprimir y compartir.

Digital guest book template: an Airbnb welcome book as a Canva website your guests open on their phone. Twelve pages, a QR code, three looks, free to publish. Getting in, parking, the house manual, rules, safety, nearby and the checkout list, with a tile menu on the front and a page menu on every page, so a guest at the door is two taps from Getting in.

FOR NIGHTLY AND MONTHLY STAYS
Written for Airbnbs and vacation rentals as well as furnished rentals let by the month. Weekend guests get check-in, the pool or hot tub, house rules and checkout in one tap. Monthly guests (travel nurses, corporate stays, relocations) also get the extras most host guidebooks skip: trash day, mail, laundry, parking passes and quiet hours.

WHAT'S ON THE PAGES
Welcome with four quick facts and the tile menu. Before you arrive. Getting in. Parking. The house. House manual. Pool and amenities. House rules. Safety. Nearby. Checkout. Need anything?

SAFE TO SHARE
Anyone with the link can open it, so the template keeps your street address and door codes OFF the page and tells the guest where to find them instead. Most welcome books get this wrong.

THREE LOOKS, PICK YOURS
The same 12 pages in three styles, each built on a furnished rental we run: Silver Palm (cream and sage), Canyon Lake (Hill Country sand and rust) and Coco Plum (coastal sand, sky and coral). Pick the one closest to your place.

HOW IT WORKS
After purchase you download a PDF with the three Canva template links and the publishing steps, a zip of all 36 finished screens, and a starter text file for drafting on your phone. Click a link, Canva makes your own copy, type over the prompts, then Share, Publish website, switch the page menu on, and publish to a free Canva address. Share the link or the QR code in your booking messages. A free Canva account is enough, and one account can publish five rentals.

GOOD TO KNOW
You don't need Canva Pro. Guests can only view the pages, not edit them. Sites on a free Canva address show a small "Designed with Canva" footer; publishing on your own domain removes it. Built for phones, and it still reads on a laptop.

results.description:
**Quick Start and Detailed Guide Videos are now on Youtube!**

After MANY suggestions I should sell this on Etsy, my planner is finally on Etsy. Most popular finance spreadsheet on Reddit. Many people have given me great feedback on this. It has everything you need and none of what you don’t need. This is a budgeting SYSTEM, not just a tracking tool. Includes YouTube tutorials explaining how to use it. 

Take control of your money with a comprehensive budgeting system designed to help you plan, track, and understand your finances for an entire year. This workbook was created entirely by me by hand. No AI. Made for real people for actually managing your money! This is a blank copy of the one I have been using to manage my money for years. 

The focus is on planning ahead, not just tracking what you’ve already spent.

Map out your expected income, expenses, savings, debt payments, and financial goals across the entire year so you can see your money before you spend it. Keep an eye on your average spend per category to stay on track for the year. Enter in planned sinking fund purchases to see if they fit in your cash flow. 

You can use your plan to answer questions like:

* How much money will I have available each month?
* What will my finances look like at the end of the year?
* When can I afford a large purchase?
* How much can I put toward savings or debt?
* If I add on a $10/month subscription how will that affect my year? 
* Are there months where my expenses will be higher than usual?
* Am I on track to reach my financial goals?

What’s Included:

Annual Money Planner
Plan your income, expenses, savings, debt payments, and financial goals across all 12 months. Then track your monthly expenses and compare to your plan. 

Monthly Budget & Transaction Tracking
Dedicated monthly pages let you record your transactions and compare your actual spending against your plan. Easy to copy/paste reoccurring transactions into the next month to reduce work required. Mobile friendly for easy entry from your phone. 

Cash Flow Planner 
See how a purchase in June might change your available cash in December. Reserve money in June for December Christmas gift purchases. 

Debt Payoff Calculator
Track up to 7 debts (message me for more if needed). See how different payment amounts will change your debt payoff timeline. Planned debt payments automatically transfer to your annual money plan. 

Net Worth Tracker
Track your assets and liabilities over time and watch your overall net worth change.

More Than a Budget. It’s a system. 

Most budget templates focus primarily on tracking what you spent and have a lot of unnecessary features that just overwhelm you and visually clutter the spreadsheet. This template puts much more emphasis on planning what you’re going to do with your money and zooming out to look at the year. 

Support From Me

You’re not left to figure out the spreadsheet on your own. 

Purchase includes support from me for setup and using the template. If you need a particular feature that is not included please let me know, including other currencies. If you have questions about how a section works or need help getting your template set up, you can reach out for assistance. I also have a YouTube channel with follow-along tutorials.

Set it up once in ten minutes. Paste your bank statement whenever you feel like it. Everything else — twelve monthly budgets, the bill calendar, your debt payoff dates, your net worth — fills itself in.

The Ultimate Budget is a 32-tab annual budget spreadsheet built on one transaction ledger. You type something once and it lands everywhere it belongs. It opens in Excel and in Google Sheets, and both are the same file with the same features.

─────────────────────────────

YOUR FIRST TEN MINUTES

1 · Name your accounts — checking, savings, cash, the credit cards.
2 · Pick your pay rhythm — weekly, bi-weekly, semi-monthly, monthly, or irregular if your income moves around.
3 · Confirm your categories — six groups are already filled in and pre-tagged 50/30/20. Edit them or leave them.
4 · List what repeats — rent, salary, the gym, the streaming you forgot about. Nine frequencies to choose from.

The moment you finish, a full year of dated payments generates itself, twelve monthly tabs populate, and the bill calendar knows what leaves your account and when.

EVERY WEEK AFTER THAT

Export the CSV your bank already gives you. Paste it into the Import tab. Your rules do the rest — TESCO becomes Groceries, NETFLIX becomes Subscriptions, and anything the file doesn't recognise waits in a short queue with a dropdown. About ninety seconds.

No monthly fee. No add-on to install. No macro to enable. It is formulas all the way down, which is exactly why it behaves the same in Excel and in Sheets.

Most budget spreadsheets make you type a savings transfer into the log, and then type it again into the savings tab. On the best-selling one, four of the wealth tabs say inside the file itself that they are not connected to anything.

Ours are. All of them.

→ Tag a transaction Emergency Fund and that fund's progress bar moves.
→ Pay a credit card and the debt payoff date moves.

Dashboard · Annual Totals · Distribution · 50/30/20

Paycheck · Calendar · Payments · Variable

Subscriptions — what renews in the next 30 days, the cancel-by date, and what each one really costs you per year

Debt Payoff — snowball, avalanche or your own order, with real dates attached

"Am I getting ahead or just busy?"
Net Worth · Sinking Funds · Investment

"Can I do better next month?"
Jan through Dec, budget against actual · No-Spend Challenge · Print Pack

None of those answers need updating. They read from the same ledger you already filled.

Room for 3,000 scheduled payments and 1,000 one-off entries a year, 15 savings goals, and every account and debt you have. Start your budget in any month — January or the middle of July — and duplicate the file each year to start clean.

─────────────────────────────

AN HONEST FIT CHECK

Buy this if you want one file that holds a whole year, you like seeing it on a dashboard, and you're willing to spend ten minutes up front so the next twelve months cost you almost nothing.

Skip it if you want something you fill in on your phone on the bus — 32 tabs is a desktop experience. Skip it too if you want three boxes and a total. This is a proper system, and that is more than some people need.

A step-by-step guide PDF
A walkthrough video

results.title: Ultimate Annual Budget Spreadsheet Excel | Google Sheets Budget Template Monthly Budget Tracker Financial Planner Bill Tracker Debt Tracker
results.description:
Set it up once in ten minutes. Paste your bank statement whenever you feel like it. Everything else — twelve monthly budgets, the bill calendar, your debt payoff dates, your net worth — fills itself in.

The Ultimate Budget is a 32-tab annual budget spreadsheet built on one transaction ledger. You type something once and it lands everywhere it belongs. It opens in Excel and in Google Sheets, and both are the same file with the same features.

─────────────────────────────

YOUR FIRST TEN MINUTES

1 · Name your accounts — checking, savings, cash, the credit cards.
2 · Pick your pay rhythm — weekly, bi-weekly, semi-monthly, monthly, or irregular if your income moves around.
3 · Confirm your categories — six groups are already filled in and pre-tagged 50/30/20. Edit them or leave them.
4 · List what repeats — rent, salary, the gym, the streaming you forgot about. Nine frequencies to choose from.

The moment you finish, a full year of dated payments generates itself, twelve monthly tabs populate, and the bill calendar knows what leaves your account and when.

EVERY WEEK AFTER THAT

Export the CSV your bank already gives you. Paste it into the Import tab. Your rules do the rest — TESCO becomes Groceries, NETFLIX becomes Subscriptions, and anything the file doesn't recognise waits in a short queue with a dropdown. About ninety seconds.

No monthly fee. No add-on to install. No macro to enable. It is formulas all the way down, which is exactly why it behaves the same in Excel and in Sheets.

─────────────────────────────

THE PART EVERY OTHER TEMPLATE GETS WRONG

Most budget spreadsheets make you type a savings transfer into the log, and then type it again into the savings tab. On the best-selling one, four of the wealth tabs say inside the file itself that they are not connected to anything.

Ours are. All of them.

→ Tag a transaction Emergency Fund and that fund's progress bar moves.
→ Pay a credit card and the debt payoff date moves.
→ Add an account and your net worth updates.

One entry, nothing typed twice. That is the whole design, and everything else follows from it.

Then the unglamorous things nobody bothers to do: headers frozen on all 32 tabs, print areas set on all 32 tabs, a filterable transaction log, every cell you're meant to type in highlighted and every formula protected so you can't break it by accident, and a linked index so you're never hunting for a tab.

─────────────────────────────

WHAT YOU CAN ACTUALLY ASK IT

"Where did the money go this month?"
Dashboard · Annual Totals · Distribution · 50/30/20

"Will I make it to payday?"
Paycheck · Calendar · Payments · Variable

"What is quietly draining me?"
Subscriptions — what renews in the next 30 days, the cancel-by date, and what each one really costs you per year

"When will this card finally be gone?"
Debt Payoff — snowball, avalanche or your own order, with real dates attached

"Am I getting ahead or just busy?"
Net Worth · Sinking Funds · Investment

"Can I do better next month?"
Jan through Dec, budget against actual · No-Spend Challenge · Print Pack

None of those answers need updating. They read from the same ledger you already filled.

Room for 3,000 scheduled payments and 1,000 one-off entries a year, 15 savings goals, and every account and debt you have. Start your budget in any month — January or the middle of July — and duplicate the file each year to start clean.

─────────────────────────────

AN HONEST FIT CHECK

Buy this if you want one file that holds a whole year, you like seeing it on a dashboard, and you're willing to spend ten minutes up front so the next twelve months cost you almost nothing.

Skip it if you want something you fill in on your phone on the bus — 32 tabs is a desktop experience. Skip it too if you want three boxes and a total. This is a proper system, and that is more than some people need.

─────────────────────────────

WHAT ARRIVES

The Excel file (.xlsx), ready to type into
A one-click link to copy the Google Sheets version into your own Drive
A step-by-step guide PDF
A walkthrough video

Instant download as soon as payment clears — from your Etsy purchases page, or the link in your receipt email if you don't have an account. Google Sheets needs a free Google account. Excel needs nothing but Excel.

Add a guest once and they appear on your seating plan, your plate counts, your save-the-date print run and your RSVP totals. Enter your wedding date once and every task on the timeline works out its own due date and drops onto your calendar. Every real payment is logged in ONE place. Your budget, your remaining balance, your overdue list and your dashboard all read that one place. You never type a number twice and you can never end up with two different answers to "what have we actually spent?"

- PRIVACY POLICY

This policy describes what personal information I collect when you buy from
this shop, why I collect it, how long I keep it, and the rights you have over it.

WHO IS RESPONSIBLE FOR YOUR DATA

The data controller is [ton nom légal complet], trading as Oakfold Documents,
[ton adresse professionnelle complète], France. You can reach me for any privacy
question through Etsy Messages or at [ton adresse e mail].

WHAT I COLLECT

Everything in this shop is a digital download, so I collect very little. When you
place an order, Etsy passes me your name, your Etsy username, the details of what
you ordered, your billing country, and the messages you send me.

I do not receive or need a shipping address, because nothing is posted to you. I
do not receive your card number or your bank details at any point. Payment is
handled entirely by Etsy and its payment processors.

WHY I COLLECT IT, AND ON WHAT LEGAL BASIS

To fulfil your order, deliver your files and answer your questions. Legal basis:
performance of the contract between us.

To meet my accounting and tax obligations, including keeping records of sales.
Legal basis: compliance with a legal obligation.

To resolve a dispute, investigate a duplicate charge or prevent fraud. Legal
basis: my legitimate interest in running the shop properly, balanced against your
rights.

To send you a message you have specifically asked for. Legal basis: your consent,
which you can withdraw at any time.

I do not send marketing messages, and I do not add buyers to any mailing list.
Etsy prohibits unsolicited messages and I agree with that rule.

WHO ELSE SEES YOUR INFORMATION

Etsy, as the platform hosting this shop and processing payments.

The tax and accounting authorities, and my accountant, where the law requires
records to be produced.

Nobody else. I do not sell, rent or share buyer information with anyone, for any
purpose.

TRANSFERS OUTSIDE THE EUROPEAN UNION

Etsy is based in the United States, so information passing through the platform
is transferred there. Etsy relies on the EU US Data Privacy Framework and on
standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission to protect those
transfers. I hold no buyer information outside the European Union myself.

HOW LONG I KEEP IT

Order and accounting records are kept for ten years, as French commercial law
requires.

Messages exchanged with you are kept for three years after our last contact, so
that I can help if you come back with a question about a file you bought.

Anything not covered by those two cases is deleted as soon as it is no longer
needed.

YOUR RIGHTS

You have the right to ask me for a copy of the information I hold about you, to
have it corrected if it is wrong, to have it deleted, to restrict or object to
how I use it, and to receive it in a portable format. Where I rely on your
consent, you can withdraw it at any time.

Some information cannot be deleted on request, because the law requires me to
keep accounting records for ten years. I will tell you plainly if that applies.

Write to me through Etsy Messages or at [ton adresse e mail]. I answer within
thirty days, and usually within twenty four hours.

If you are not satisfied with my answer, you can complain to the supervisory
authority of your country. For France that is the CNIL, at www.cnil.fr.

WHAT SOFTWARE DO I NEED TO EDIT THE CONTRACTS AND FORMS?
Nothing you have to buy. Every kit for small service businesses comes as a fillable PDF that opens in the free Adobe Acrobat Reader, in Preview on a Mac or in Chrome, and as editable Word files that open in Microsoft Word, Google Docs, Pages and the free LibreOffice. Put your business name and logo on the contracts, quotes, invoices and client forms, change any wording, and export your own PDF. No Canva account, no subscription, no design app.

CAN I USE THESE FORMS FOR MY OWN CLIENTS AND MY OWN BUSINESS?
Yes. Every contract, quote, invoice, checklist and client form is licensed for your own commercial use with as many clients as you need, for as long as you need, with no per use fee and no expiry. Cleaning businesses, contractors, handymen, childcare and event vendors use them every day. What you may not do is resell, share or redistribute the files, edited or not, or put them in a bundle or course of your own. The full terms are on the last page of each PDF.

MY CLIENTS DO NOT READ ENGLISH. CAN I TRANSLATE THE FORMS?
Yes, and that is why the Word files are included. Translate them once into the language you work in, in Word or with the translate tool in Google Docs, correct the wording yourself, save them, and use them for every client after that. The layout survives translation. The kits are written in plain English so that the translation stays readable, and every page exists in US Letter and A4 so the print size is right wherever you are.

results.title: Paycheck to Paycheck Budget Planner | Paycheck Budget Spreadsheet | Biweekly Budget Planner | Excel + Google Sheets
results.description:
**Stop guessing where your paycheck went. Give every dollar of every paycheck a job — before you spend it.**

If you're living paycheck to paycheck, a monthly budget never quite fits — your bills don't land on the 1st, and neither does your pay. The **Paycheck-to-Paycheck Budget Planner** is the beginner-friendly spreadsheet built around how you actually get paid: pick your pay frequency, list your bills once, assign each bill to the paycheck that covers it, and see exactly what's left over per paycheck — before it's gone.

### Why it's different
- **📅 Built around paydays, not months** — Weekly, biweekly, semimonthly, or monthly: enter your next payday and net pay, and the next 12 paychecks date themselves automatically. Semimonthly uses the true yearly average so spacing stays honest.
- **💵 Every bill assigned to a paycheck** — List up to 30 bills with category and due-day dropdowns, then tag each one with the paycheck (1–12) it comes out of. Each paycheck's bills total themselves — no mental math.
- **🎯 Savings + spending targets per paycheck** — Set what you want to save and what you're allowed to spend from each check. Leftover calculates itself and lights up green when healthy, red when a paycheck is over budget.
- **🚨 Over-budget flags** — Any paycheck where bills + savings + spending exceed your pay gets flagged "⚠ Over budget" automatically, so you can move a bill or trim spending before payday hits.
- **📊 Dashboard that tells the truth** — Total income vs. bills across all 12 paychecks, your savings rate as a percentage, bills ranked by category, your largest bill, and a check that flags any bill missing a paycheck assignment.
- **🚀 5-minute setup** — Plain-language START HERE tab. Pale teal cells are yours to fill; everything else calculates automatically. No finance jargon.

### What's included (instant download)
1. **Paycheck-to-Paycheck Budget Planner workbook** (Excel .xlsx — also imports cleanly into Google Sheets): 5 tabs — START HERE, PAYCHECK SETUP (12 auto-dated paychecks), BILLS (30 bills with category/due-day/paycheck dropdowns), PAYCHECK PLAN (per-paycheck bills, savings, spending, leftover, status flags), DASHBOARD (totals, savings rate, category ranking, assignment check)
2. **README** with setup instructions

### How it works
1. Download your files instantly after checkout.
2. On PAYCHECK SETUP, pick your pay frequency and enter your next payday + net pay.
3. List your bills on the BILLS tab and assign each to a paycheck (1–12).
4. On PAYCHECK PLAN, set savings and spending-money targets per paycheck — leftover and status flags do the rest.

### FAQ
**I get paid biweekly but my partner gets paid monthly. Can this handle both?**
Set it up for your own paychecks first — that's the core of the plan. You can run a second copy of the file for a second income stream; the 12-paycheck layout works for any single frequency.

**Excel or Google Sheets?**
Both. The file is an .xlsx that opens in Excel and imports cleanly into Google Sheets (File → Import).

**What if a bill is due before the paycheck I assigned it to?**
The planner assigns bills by paycheck, not by date — the due-day column is your at-a-glance check. If a bill lands earlier than its paycheck, assign it to the earlier paycheck instead.

**How is this different from a monthly budget spreadsheet?**
Monthly budgets assume all your money arrives at once. This one plans each paycheck as its own mini-budget — which is the only budget that works when money is tight between paydays.

**Is this a physical product?**
No — this is a digital download. No physical item will be shipped.

A thoughtful last-minute gift for anyone starting their money reset. Heading into the holidays, it's the perfect tool to map every bill against every paycheck *before* the seasonal spending starts — so December's subscriptions and January's statements never catch you off guard.

Paid weekly, every two weeks or twice a month? A monthly budget never quite fits. This one is built around your pay period. Tell it one payday and it lays out every pay period for you, shows what each paycheck has to cover, and moves on to the next one by itself.

THE QUESTIONS IT ANSWERS

How much can I spend today?
"Left to spend" and "Safe to spend per day" sit at the top of the page. The daily number is what is left of your spending plan, spread over the days until your next payday.

Which bills come out of this paycheck?
Type each bill once, with the day of the month it is due. The page works out which pay period that day falls in. Rent on the 1st shows up in the paycheck that covers the 1st, not in every paycheck.

Did I pay it?
Log a bill and it turns to Paid. Until then you see "Due in 4 days", "Due today" or "Overdue". Paid a few days early or late? It still counts for its due date.

Will the next paycheck be short?
The page looks one pay period ahead. If rent week is coming, it tells you how much to keep back from this paycheck.

Am I sticking to the plan?
Planned next to actual for money in, bills, spending, savings and debt, with a bar for each and a chart of where the money goes.

How did my last paychecks go?
Your last six pay periods sit side by side: money in, money out, saved, left over, and your average.

results.description:
A budget by paycheck: every paycheck of the year, with the bills it has to cover, the money to set aside for sinking funds, your spending money and what is left over. Set up your pay once and every bill lands under the paycheck that comes before it is due. Use it in Google Sheets (free) or Excel.

WHAT'S INCLUDED
• Setup: weekly, every 2 weeks, twice a month or monthly pay, a second paycheck on its own schedule (for couples), a weekend payday rule, other monthly income (child support, a side job) and spending money per paycheck
• Paychecks: every payday of the year, worked out for you. Type a real date or amount over any (a holiday, overtime)
• Bills: up to 40 bills that are monthly, every paycheck, weekly, every 2 weeks, every 3 or 6 months, yearly or once, with autopay, account, about per month and per year, and a Check column for typos
• 12 month tabs: each paycheck with its bills, sinking funds, spending money, left over and a running total. This paycheck is highlighted; mark bills Paid or Autopay as you go
• Sinking Funds: up to 12 goals (Christmas, car repairs, a vacation). Each works out what to set aside per paycheck and shows if you are on track
• Spending Log: purchases by category; every month compares them with your spending money

This Paycheck Budget Spreadsheet for Google Sheets helps you organize bills by paycheck, plan weekly, biweekly, or semi-monthly income, and see your Safe-to-Spend amount after planned bills, essentials, savings goals, and your chosen buffer are reserved.

Instead of trying to manage every area of your finances in one complicated spreadsheet, this focused Budget by Paycheck system answers the question that matters every payday:

“Which bills does this paycheck need to cover, and what can I safely spend after that?”

PAYCHECK PLANNING MADE CLEAR

Enter your pay schedule and recurring bills once, and the spreadsheet helps organize your upcoming paychecks and planned commitments.

✓ Weekly, biweekly, and semi-monthly (twice-monthly) pay schedules

✓ Paycheck-to-Bill Map showing which bills are funded by each paycheck

✓ Suggested paycheck assignments based on bill funding deadlines

✓ Manual override when you prefer to fund a bill from an earlier paycheck

✓ Safe-to-Spend calculation after planned commitments

✓ Bill Calendar for a clear monthly overview

✓ Payday Dashboard with paycheck allocation chart

✓ Eight-paycheck forward outlook

✓ Automatically matched bill list for each payday

✓ Short-paycheck warnings

✓ Alerts when a bill is assigned to a paycheck after its funding deadline

✓ Optional savings and extra debt-payment goals

YOUR PAYCHECK GETS A JOB BEFORE YOU SPEND IT

The system helps you reserve money in this order:

Bills
Everyday essentials
Your chosen buffer
Optional savings or extra debt-payment goals
Extra spending

What remains becomes your Safe-to-Spend amount.

This gives you a clearer picture of how much of each paycheck is actually available instead of assuming the full account balance is spendable.

PLAN YOUR BILLS BY PAYCHECK

Add recurring bills with their:

• Bill name
• Amount
• Due date
• Recurrence pattern
• Funding timing

The spreadsheet generates upcoming bill occurrences and suggests which paycheck should fund each one.

Prefer to pay or reserve money earlier?

You can override the suggested assignment and choose another paycheck.

The system also flags bills assigned too late, helping you catch potential planning problems before the due date arrives.

PAYDAY DASHBOARD

View:

• Selected paycheck amount
• Bills reserved
• Essentials reserve
• Buffer
• Goals
• Extra spending

Use the Goals tab for:

• Savings contributions
• Extra debt payments
• Goal targets

Indica cómo cobras (cada semana, cada 2 semanas, dos veces al mes o una vez al mes) y escribe tus facturas una sola vez. El archivo calcula tus fechas de cobro de los próximos 12 meses, asigna cada factura a la nómina que la paga y te muestra cuánto dinero para gastar deja cada nómina, de modo que una nómina posterior no se quede corta.

3 TEMAS DE COLOR INCLUIDOS (BOLD, SOFT, DARK)
Bold (negro y amarillo, el tema por defecto), Soft (menta y lila en tonos pastel) y Dark (gris oscuro con amarillo). Es el mismo libro con las mismas fórmulas y el mismo ejemplo: solo cambian los colores y el tipo de letra. Cada tema es un archivo independiente, así que abre el que más te guste.

QUÉ HACE
- Fechas de cobro para 12 meses: semanal, cada 2 semanas, dos veces al mes o mensual. Si un cobro cae en fin de semana o en un festivo bancario, se mueve al día laborable anterior (o al siguiente, tú eliges). Los festivos bancarios de EE. UU. de 2026 a 2030 ya están rellenados; añade los tuyos.
- Hasta 2 personas con ingresos en un solo plan del hogar, cada una con su propio calendario de cobro. Dos ingresos en un mismo plan; no reparte los gastos entre las dos. Una factura puede pagarla una persona o cualquiera de las dos.
- Cada factura va a la última nómina que llega antes de su fecha de vencimiento. Un alquiler mayor que una nómina se puede pagar mitad con cada una de 2 nóminas. Mueve una factura solo por un mes en la pestaña Bill moves.
- Paycheck plan (plan de nóminas): elige un mes y verás una tarjeta por nómina con sus facturas, gastos semanales, ahorro, dinero que guardar para una nómina posterior y tu dinero para gastar, marcada como Covered (cubierta) o Short (corta).
- Dashboard (panel): "Safe to spend until your next payday" (lo que puedes gastar hasta tu próximo cobro; escribe el saldo de tu cuenta para verlo en vivo), totales de 12 meses, próxima nómina, próximas facturas, una tabla por meses y gráficos.
- Los meses con nómina extra se señalan (3 nóminas cada 2 semanas o 5 semanales en un mismo mes). Esa nómina puede quedar libre de facturas con fecha, de modo que ese dinero es de verdad extra.
- Los gastos semanales, como la compra o la gasolina, se reparten entre tus nóminas.
- Fondos de ahorro (hasta 15) con una meta y una fecha, o con una cantidad fija por nómina.
- Pay log (registro de cobros) para lo que has cobrado de verdad, Bill tracker (control de facturas) para marcar facturas pagadas (escribe x) y Bill calendar (calendario de facturas) con cada fecha de vencimiento y la nómina que la paga.
- Avisos claros y una pestaña Help (ayuda) con 21 preguntas respondidas.

QUÉ RECIBES (descarga instantánea)
1. Tres libros de Excel, uno por cada tema de color: Paycheck-Budget-Planner-v1.1-Bold.xlsx, Paycheck-Budget-Planner-v1.1-Soft.xlsx y Paycheck-Budget-Planner-v1.1-Dark.xlsx. CÓMO FUNCIONA
1. Setup: cómo cobras, un día de cobro normal y tu sueldo neto; una segunda persona si dos comparten el plan; el dinero inicial y el primer mes.
2. Bills: una fila por factura, con nombre, importe y día de vencimiento. Hasta 40 facturas.
3. Savings: metas opcionales con una cantidad y una fecha.
4. Mira tu plan en Paycheck plan y Dashboard.
5. Cada día de cobro, introduce el importe en Pay log solo si difiere del previsto; si no introduces ninguno, se usa el previsto. Marca las facturas pagadas en Bill tracker.
Solo las celdas de color amarillo claro sirven para escribir, en los tres temas. En los archivos de Excel las fórmulas están protegidas sin contraseña, así que puedes desproteger una hoja si quieres cambiar algo. En tu copia de Google Sheets las celdas con fórmula están configuradas para pedir confirmación antes de un cambio.

COMPATIBILIDAD

```
results.title: Biweekly Budget Spreadsheet Excel Google Sheets, Paycheck Cash Flow Planner, Monthly Budget Template with Daily Balance Tracker
results.description:
```
Almost every budget spreadsheet on here works in months. Add up income for the month, add up spending for the month, subtract. On the worked household inside this workbook that arithmetic says the year clears $9,422. Nothing about that sentence is wrong.

But nobody is paid in months. Someone on biweekly pay is paid every fourteen days, and 365 days does not divide evenly into twelve months. It divides into 26 pay periods, not 24, so two months a year carry three paychecks instead of two. And the account itself does not experience the month closing. It experiences the days in between, in order, and on the worked household the balance falls to negative $2,205 on 05 January, three days before that year's first paycheck arrives.

WHAT IT IS
A day by day cash flow simulator plus a monthly budget, in Excel and Google Sheets. Eight tabs. You enter your pay, your bills with their due day, your typical spending, and your annual costs. It builds a full year of your own calendar, one day at a time, and shows you the one week a monthly total cannot see.

WHAT'S INSIDE
- Setup: your first payday, your paycheck amount, your starting cushion, two candidate savings transfer dates
- Categories and Costs: monthly bills with due days, per paycheck spending, annual and irregular costs
- Day by Day Cash Flow: every day of the year, income and outgoings, running balance, built for you
- Monthly Budget: the same year added up by category and by month, the familiar view
- Cash Flow Findings: the buffer, the trough, the days below zero, both savings dates counted
- Dashboard: the whole year on one screen
- How To Use

WHY IT'S DIFFERENT
It runs your actual calendar twice against two candidate savings transfer dates and counts the days each one costs you. On the worked household the buffer needed is identical either way, because it is set by the household's bills and pay dates alone. What moves is the number of days the balance spends below zero, which is a property of the household's own saving habit. Neither date is recommended. Both are counted.

• A blank workbook for your own budget and a filled-in sample workbook for a made-up household, so you can see how every tab works. The sample is paid every 2 weeks and has 432 transactions logged for January to September 2027.

Then set up your budget categories: each has a group (needs, wants, or savings and debt) and a plan per paycheck for the ones you fund from every paycheck. The workbook works out every payday in your 12-month plan year.
• Paychecks: every payday in the plan year, with the dates it covers, your income, the bills due, your spending plan and savings plan, and what is left to budget. Type a real amount in a cream cell when a paycheck is different. Extra paychecks in a month are shaded, and a paycheck that comes up short shows in red.
• Bills: 40 recurring bills (monthly, every 3 months, every 6 months, or yearly). For each one, enter a name, category, amount, due day, how often it repeats, and whether it is on autopay. The workbook places every bill in the paycheck that covers its due date.
• Paycheck Plan: type a paycheck number to see its income, the bills due before the next payday, your spending and savings plan next to what you spent in that pay period, and what is left to budget.
• Bill Calendar: choose a month to see each bill on the day it is due and each payday marked. Cards show what is due, what is on autopay, and the paydays in the month, and a list shows every bill in date order with the paycheck that covers it.
• Transactions: a log with 2,500 rows for what you spend, bill payments included. Enter the date, where or what, category, amount, account, and notes, and pick the category and the account from dropdowns. The tab works out which paycheck covers each date.
• Monthly Budget: choose a month to compare budget, spent, and left by group and by category, with a bar for each category. A category that went over budget turns red.
• Savings Goals: 10 goals, each with a target amount, an optional target date, and a starting balance. It works out what you have saved, what is left to go, your progress, the paydays left before the date, and what each paycheck needs to make the date. A status tells you if your plan is on pace for the date or short of it.
• Dashboard: eight cards for income, budgeted, spent so far, left to budget, bills for the year, paychecks, saved toward goals, and budget used. A chart shows income, budget, and spending by month, a ring chart shows where the budget goes, and you also get your top spending categories and your savings goals with progress bars.
• Year Summary: all 12 months side by side, with paydays, income, bills, plans, budget, and spending, then the budget and the spending for every category by month. Bill Schedule: every bill in every plan month, with its due date and the paycheck that covers it. There is nothing to type on either tab.
• How much it holds: up to 54 paychecks in a plan year (weekly, every 2 weeks, twice a month, or monthly); 40 recurring bills; 30 budget categories (25 filled in, all editable), in 3 groups; 2,500 transaction rows; 10 savings goals; and 8 accounts
• Time span: 12 months, starting with the month of your first payday. It is not tied to a calendar year, so you can start in any month. Save a fresh copy of the blank file to start a new plan year.

HOW IT WORKS
1. Download the two files after you buy: a zip file (it holds the blank workbook, the filled-in sample workbook, and the Start Here PDF) and the Start Here PDF on its own.
2. To use Excel, open the zip file (on Windows, right-click it and choose Extract All; on a Mac, double-click it), then open the blank workbook from the extracted folder. To use Google Sheets, open the Start Here PDF, click the link for the blank workbook, and choose Make a copy.
3. On the Settings tab, type your first payday, choose how often you are paid, and type your take-home pay. Then give each category you fund from every paycheck a plan per paycheck, and list your recurring bills on the Bills tab with the day of the month each one is due. Type only in the cream cells.

A monthly budget assumes rent, groceries, and the car insurance all wait until the 1st. They don't.

Who this is for

People in the US, UK, Australia, and Canada who are paid weekly or every two weeks. Hourly, salaried, retail, healthcare, trades, dual-income households with mismatched pay dates. You tried a monthly template. You still had a week where the checking account was empty and a bill was not.

This also works if you are paid semi-monthly or monthly. Weekly and biweekly is where monthly budgets quietly fail.

The problem

A monthly budget lies when your money arrives in chunks. Rent hits one check. The car insurance hits another. A three-paycheck month looks like a surplus until you spend it, then February has three bills and two checks.

This kit assigns every bill to a specific paycheck. You look at one check, you see what it has to cover, and you see what is left. That is the whole idea.

4. This Paycheck — the product: split this check into bills, sinking funds, debt, leftover
5. Next Paychecks — map the next 4–6 checks so a three-paycheck month does not surprise you
6. Transactions — log what actually left the account
7. Bill Calendar — which check pays which bill
8. Sinking Funds — 20 named funds (car repair, Christmas, rent deposit, vet, insurance deductible, medical, gifts, vacation, kids' activities, home maintenance, new tires, back to school, birthdays, emergency, furniture, clothing, pets, subscriptions, property tax, other)
9. Debt Snowball — balances, minimum payment, extra, projected payoff order
10. Monthly vs Actual — the month against what you planned
11. Year Overview — undated. Works this year, next year, and the year after that.

Input cells are the yellow ones. Formula cells are locked. You do not need to know spreadsheets. You need to know your take-home pay and when the bills come out.

The printable PDF (22 pages)

For the weeks you want paper. Low ink. Fillable lines.

Paycheck planning sheets, monthly budget, bill checklist, 20-fund sinking tracker, debt snowball worksheet, annual overview, a Sunday money-date one-pager, extra logs. US Letter (8.5 × 11 in) and A4 (210 × 297 mm) are both in the ZIP.

Paycheck budget spreadsheet and biweekly budget planner: budget by paycheck, then watch your debt disappear.

This paycheck budget spreadsheet for Google Sheets and Excel turns weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly or monthly pay into one clear monthly budget, then uses the debt snowball or debt avalanche to show the exact month you will be debt free. A zero based budget, bill tracker, expense tracker, subscription tracker, sinking fund savings tracker, debt payoff tracker and net worth tracker in one personal finance spreadsheet - beginner friendly, with the free guide walking you through setup.

BUDGET BY PAYCHECK

Most monthly budget templates assume one paycheck a month. This paycheck budget tracker asks how often you are paid and does the conversion for you, so weekly budgeting and biweekly budgeting both land on a real monthly budget. Give every dollar a job until "Left to assign" reads zero. Enter a bill's due day once and it tells you which paycheck covers it. Yearly subscriptions show as a real monthly cost.

THEN IT KILLS THE DEBT

Enter each balance, APR and minimum, choose Snowball or Avalanche from a dropdown, add whatever extra you can afford, and the sheet plays the whole thing forward month by month for ten years. Every time a debt clears, its minimum rolls onto the next one, so your total payment never shrinks. You get the month you are debt free and the total interest you will pay. Flip the dropdown to the other strategy and both figures update in a second, so you can see which one saves you more.

WHAT IS IN IT - 13 TABS

Start Here - Paycheck Budget - Paycheck Log - Bills - Subscriptions - Spending Log - Debts - Payoff Plan - Payoff Summary - Savings Goals - Net Worth - Category Summary - Dashboard

The Dashboard pulls every figure from the tabs before it. There is nothing to fill in on it. Five cards across the top show your monthly take-home, what is left to assign, your total debt, the months until you are debt free and your net worth. The Category Summary puts budget against actual spending for every category, like a financial planner that keeps itself up to date.

WHAT YOU GET

- The spreadsheet (.xlsx, 13 linked tabs) plus a free 9-page PDF quick start guide, instant download

- No add-ons, no macros, no subscription, nothing to install
- Bold, bright colors: deep plum, hot pink and lavender, with its own color for every kind of tab

CAPACITY

24 budget categories, 60 paydays, 40 bills, 25 subscriptions, 300 spending entries, 12 debts, 20 savings goals, 18 assets and 18 liabilities, and a 120-month payoff plan. Every total counts exactly these rows - a row typed below the last one is not counted.

THINGS IT DOES THAT MOST DO NOT

- Converts weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly and monthly pay to a real monthly figure
- Tells you which paycheck each bill falls on, from the due day
- Rolls every cleared minimum onto the next debt automatically

- Says "Over 120 months" rather than printing a payoff date it cannot stand behind

results.title: Paycheck Budget, Biweekly Budget Spreadsheet, Semi Monthly Budget Planner, Budget by Paycheck, Income Tracker, Excel Google Sheets
results.description:
Paycheck budget spreadsheet for Excel and Google Sheets. A biweekly budget, semi monthly budget planner and weekly pay plan in one file: every bill placed on the paycheck that pays it, fifty-two paychecks ahead from your first 2026 payday. Change one date and the whole plan rolls forward.

Rent is due on the 1st. You get paid on the 28th and again on the 11th. The phone bill lands on the 16th, the car payment on the 4th, and twice a year car insurance turns up in the same fortnight as everything else.

A monthly budget adds all of that up and tells you the month is fine. The month may well be fine. The paycheck on the 28th is not, because it is carrying rent, the loan and the insurance on its own while the next one carries almost nothing.

This file plans the way your money actually arrives: paycheck by paycheck. Type each bill once, say how often it repeats, and every repeat lands on the paycheck that has to cover it.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

SEE A FULL PLAN WORKING BEFORE YOU TYPE A SINGLE BILL

An empty budget tells you nothing about whether it will work for you. So the download includes a second copy of the workbook that has already been filled in for a household paid every two weeks.

Seventeen bills, from rent and groceries to a twice-a-year insurance premium and a one-time holiday budget. Fifty-two paychecks from January 2026 to December 2027, every one of them with its bills placed, its left-over money worked out, and a Covered or Short verdict. Three of those paychecks come back Short, exactly as they would in a real household, so you can see what the warning looks like and why it appeared.

Open it first. Click through the six tabs. Within a couple of minutes you will know how a bill finds its paycheck, what the grid on Pay Periods is telling you and whether this is the plan you want. Then open the empty copy and start with your own payday.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

WHAT YOU GET

- Paycheck Budget Spreadsheet.xlsx: your empty working copy
- Paycheck Budget Spreadsheet - DEMO.xlsx: the same workbook with a full example household already in it
- START HERE.pdf: one page telling you which file to open first and how to open it in Excel or Google Sheets

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

WHAT IS INSIDE: SIX TABS

1. DASHBOARD
Where this paycheck stands, worked out from today's date. The next payday and how many days away it is. The bills that fall on the current paycheck and what is left over after them. Whether the essential bills are covered this period. The lowest your balance gets across all fifty-two paychecks, and on which date. A table and chart of the next twelve paychecks against their bills, and a line of the balance ahead across the whole plan. Nothing on this tab is typed.

2. SET UP
Pay frequency from a dropdown: Weekly, Biweekly or Twice a month. Your first pay date, your net pay per paycheck and your starting balance. For twice-a-month pay, the two days of the month you are paid. Currency symbol for the headings. The pay date cell only accepts dates, and in Google Sheets it opens a calendar when you click it.

3. BILLS
Thirty rows, one per bill, typed once. Amount. Essential, yes or no. How often it repeats, from a dropdown: every paycheck, monthly, every two months, quarterly, twice a year, yearly or one time. The next due date, with a calendar in Google Sheets. Paid from: the paycheck before the due date or the one after it. The file works out what each bill costs per year and totals them. A row with an amount but no frequency or no date turns red, so nothing drops out of the plan without you noticing.

4. PAY PERIODS
All fifty-two paychecks in order: pay date, the day the period runs to, net pay, bills due, essential bills due, money left over, Covered or Short, and the running balance ahead. To the right sits the grid: one column per bill, one row per paycheck, and the amount wherever a bill lands. An empty cell means that bill is paid from a different paycheck. Nothing on this tab is typed either.

5. INSTRUCTIONS
Where to type, step by step. What the shaded cells, the red rows and the Covered or Short colours mean, and how a bill finds its paycheck.

6. PAYCHECK GUIDE
Why a paycheck plan works differently from a monthly one. Why Paid from is your choice and not the file's guess. What counts as essential. What a Short paycheck is actually telling you, and how to read the balance ahead.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT

A BILL IS TYPED ONCE, NOT ONCE PER PAYCHECK
Rent is one row for all fifty-two paychecks. Car insurance is one row with Twice a year. Groceries are one row with Every paycheck. The file places every repeat for two years ahead.

YOU DECIDE WHICH PAYCHECK PAYS
Rent due on the 1st comes out of the paycheck before it for one household and the paycheck after it for another, depending on grace periods and how tight the month is. Choose once per bill. Every repeat follows the same rule.

SHORT SHOWS UP MONTHS AHEAD
Essential bills are checked against every single paycheck, not against a monthly total. When three bills cluster on one payday, you see that paycheck marked Short today, while moving one bill is still easy.

THE GRID SHOWS YOU WHY
Every paycheck with every bill that lands on it, side by side. When a paycheck is Short, the grid shows exactly which bills met there.

THE BALANCE RUNS FORWARD
Your starting balance plus each paycheck's left-over money, in order, for all fifty-two paychecks. A dip somewhere in month eight is visible now, not when it arrives.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

WHAT THE EXAMPLE HOUSEHOLD SHOWS

The demo household is paid every two weeks, 1,850 per paycheck, and starts with 600 in the account.

Its seventeen bills cost 41,802 across a year, against 48,100 of pay. On paper that is comfortable.

Paycheck by paycheck it is not always comfortable. On May 1, 2026, rent, the student loan, internet and the water bill land on the same payday as groceries and fuel. Essential bills that period come to 2,003 against a 1,850 paycheck, so the file marks it Short.

Three of the fifty-two paychecks come back Short that way. The lowest the balance ever gets is 781, on February 6, 2026. After fifty-two paychecks it reaches 13,596.

That is the whole point of planning by paycheck: the year works, and you can still see the three paydays that need one bill moved.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

WHO IT SUITS

YOU ARE PAID EVERY TWO WEEKS
Twenty-six paychecks a year, and twice a year a month with three of them. The plan is built on the dates, so the third paycheck is simply there.

YOU ARE PAID TWICE A MONTH
Type your two paydays, the 1st and the 15th or any other pair. Short months are handled: a payday on the 30th lands on the last day of February.

YOU ARE PAID WEEKLY
Fifty-two paychecks is one full year ahead, with bills placed on the right week.

YOUR BILLS ARE NOT ALL MONTHLY
Water every other month, insurance twice a year, a registration once a year, a one-off expense in December. Each is one row.

YOU WANT TO STOP GUESSING WHICH PAYCHECK IS TIGHT
The grid and the Covered or Short column answer that for every payday at once.

YOU ARE STARTING FROM TODAY
Put today's next payday as the first pay date and your current account balance as the starting balance. The plan runs forward from there.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

HOW IT WORKS

Step 1. Open Set Up. Pick your pay frequency, then type your first pay date, net pay per paycheck and starting balance.
Step 2. Open Pay Periods. Fifty-two pay dates appear on their own. Check the first few match your real paydays.
Step 3. Go to Bills. One row per bill: amount, essential or not, how often it repeats, the next due date, and whether it is paid from the paycheck before or after that date.
Step 4. Back on Pay Periods, the grid shows every bill on the paycheck that pays it. Left over and Essential show whether each paycheck covers its bills.
Step 5. Open the Dashboard for the current paycheck and the balance ahead.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

COMPATIBILITY

✔ Microsoft Excel 2016 or newer, Windows and Mac. No account needed
✔ Google Sheets in the browser. Needs a free Google account. Upload the file and it calculates straight away, and date cells open a calendar
✔ No macros, no add-ons, no scripts
✔ Built for a computer. You can open it on a phone or tablet to check a number, but it was not designed for editing on a small screen
✘ Not built for Apple Numbers

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

COMMON QUESTIONS

How do I make a biweekly budget?
Start from your pay dates, not from the calendar. List your paydays, then place each bill on the paycheck that has to cover it: usually the last paycheck on or before the due date. Add up each paycheck's bills and take them away from its net pay. What is left is what that paycheck has for everything else.

What is the difference between a paycheck budget and a monthly budget?
A monthly budget adds up a month of income against a month of bills. A paycheck budget checks each paycheck against the bills it has to cover. Both can say the month is fine while one paycheck in it is not, and only the paycheck budget shows you which one.

Which paycheck should pay a bill?
The safe default is the last paycheck on or before the due date, so the money is already there. Some bills have a grace period of a few days, and paying them from the next paycheck spreads the load. This file lets you choose per bill.

What does semi monthly pay mean?
Paid twice a month on fixed days, for example the 1st and the 15th. That is twenty-four paychecks a year. Biweekly means every two weeks, which is twenty-six paychecks a year and a third paycheck in two months of the year.

How do I know if a paycheck will cover my bills?
Add up the essential bills that land on it and compare them with its net pay. If the bills are bigger, that paycheck is short even if the month as a whole balances. The file does this for all fifty-two paychecks and marks each one Covered or Short.

What is a starting balance for?
It is the money already in the account on your first pay date. The balance ahead starts there and adds each paycheck's left-over money in turn, so the line shows where the account is heading if nothing else changes.

Does it work in Google Sheets?
Yes. Upload the file to Google Drive and open it with Google Sheets. It calculates straight away, the dropdowns work and date cells open a calendar.

Can I use it in euros, pounds or another currency?
Yes. Type your currency symbol once on Set Up and it shows in the headings.

What if my pay changes?
Change net pay on Set Up and every paycheck, the grid totals and the balance ahead update at once.

Can I keep using it after the fifty-two paychecks?
Yes. Move the first pay date forward on Set Up and the whole plan moves with it. Repeating bills keep repeating on their own; only a one-time bill needs a new date.

Is anything locked?
No. No password, no hidden sheets, no protected cells. Every formula is visible.

Does it use macros?
No. Nothing to enable, which is also why it works the same in Google Sheets.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

WHAT IS NOT INCLUDED

It does not connect to your bank or payroll. Pay and bills are what you type.
It does not track day-to-day spending line by line. If you want a year of spending against a monthly plan, our Annual Budget Dashboard does that. If paying off debt is the goal, our Debt Payoff Calculator works out snowball and avalanche side by side.
It does not give financial advice. The example household and its numbers are a working demo, not a recommendation. Whether to move a bill, ask for a new due date or build a buffer is your decision.

DELIVERY

Instant download. Three files in a zip, available as soon as your payment goes through. This is a digital product. Nothing is posted to you.

SUPPORT
