results.title: Monthly Budget Spreadsheet for Social Security / Pension Income | Paid Once a Month Bill Planner | Fixed Income, Google Sheets & Excel
results.description:
It shows which bills fall due before your money arrives, and which months come up short.

If you are paid once a month (Social Security, a pension, an annuity) the problem is not which paycheck pays which bill. It is the bills due on the 1st, 2nd and 3rd, before the deposit lands on the 12th. Those get paid out of last month's money, and a budget that only adds up the month never shows it. This does.

THREE LISTS, THEN IT WORKS

1. Income: Social Security, pension, annuity, up to four sources, each with its amount and how it is paid.
2. Monthly bills, by the day of the month each is due. Not the date, the day. They roll forward every month.
3. Once-a-year bills (insurance, property tax) with a month and a day. They land in the right month on their own.

WHAT YOU GET BACK

A 12-month ledger: the first payday, money in, bills due before payday, bills due on or after it, what is left, and the balance at the start and end of each month. A "lowest point before payday" column turns red when the account has to already hold the money. A card at the top names the first month that comes up short. Another says how much to set aside each month for the once-a-year bills.

SOCIAL SECURITY PAY DATES ARE WORKED OUT FOR YOU

Social Security pays on a Wednesday set by your birth day: born 1st-10th is the 2nd Wednesday, 11th-20th the 3rd, 21st-31st the 4th. If you started before May 1997, or you get SSI together with Social Security, pick "paid on the 3rd" instead; a 3rd on a weekend moves to the Friday before. The sheet finds the real date for every month. Fixed-day pensions use the day you type, including the 31st in short months and the 29th in a leap-year February.

LARGE PRINT

12-point type, wide cells, high contrast, one setup tab and one results tab. It prints on landscape letter.

CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED

Every date and balance was recomputed in a separate calculation across seven scenarios (924 ledger cells), including leap-year February, a payday on the 31st, a Social Security 3rd on a weekend, a bill due on payday itself, a month that is only short at month end, and no income at all. No mismatches, no formula errors in the blank or the filled file.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO

- It does not connect to your bank. You type your own numbers in.
- It does not move a payday for a bank holiday. Fixed-day pensions show the date you typed.
- It follows one account. A bill with no due day is counted in the month total but not placed before or after payday.
- It is a planner. It does not tell you what to spend.

FORMAT AND DELIVERY

Instant download. One zip, three files: the blank Excel workbook, the same workbook filled with an example so you can see it work, and a one-page start-here sheet. Works in Excel 2016 or later. For Google Sheets, upload the file to Google Drive and open it with Google Sheets.

Personal use only. Not for resale or redistribution.

Built with AI assistance. Every figure was checked against a separate calculation before release.

results.description:
A budget spreadsheet for people who have given up on budget spreadsheets.

You type in two places: a short Setup once, then one Transactions log each time money comes in or goes out. The Dashboard, your bills, savings goals, debts and account balances all fill themselves. One log. Ten minutes. No locked cells.

ADHD-friendly by design: one place to type, three short steps, and no number you have to update twice.

━━━━━━━━━━
WHAT YOU GET · 3 FILES
━━━━━━━━━━
• Simple-Budget-Spreadsheet.xlsx: your blank budget, 12 months from any month you choose
• Simple-Budget-Spreadsheet-EXAMPLE.xlsx: the same file filled with made-up sample data (January to October 2026), so you can click around before you start
• Simple-Budget-Quick-Start-Guide.pdf (4 pages): which file to open, the 3 steps, 7 simple rules, questions and answers, and your Google Sheets "Make a copy" link

━━━━━━━━━━
7 TABS
━━━━━━━━━━
• Start Here: three steps and short tips, with a link to each tab
• Setup: first month, year and currency symbol, then up to 6 income sources, 24 spending categories, 6 savings goals, 6 debts, 6 accounts and 15 monthly bills
• Transactions: the one log you fill in. Date, payee, category, amount, account, a "to account" for transfers, a ✔ column for rows that have reached your bank, and a note. 1,500 rows ready.
• Dashboard: pick a month and see money in, money out, saved + debt paid and safe to spend, a "where the money went" chart, budget vs spent for each category, bills marked Paid ✔ / Due / Overdue, savings goals, debts and account balances
• Year: 12 months side by side with totals, monthly averages, money left over and a column chart
• Accounts: the balance of each account plus a quick check against your bank
• Lists: the automatic lists behind the drop-downs (no need to touch)

━━━━━━━━━━
WHY IT'S SIMPLE
━━━━━━━━━━
• A payee column. You see who you paid, not only the category.
• Bills tick themselves off. Give each bill a name in Setup, use that name as the payee when you pay it, and the Dashboard shows Paid ✔. No separate recurring tab to match up.
• A built-in bank check. Type what your bank app shows and the Accounts tab shows the difference. The ✔ column tells you which rows haven't reached your bank yet.
• Nothing is locked. No passwords, no macros. Click any grey cell to see its formula.
• No video needed. The Start Here tab and the 4-page guide cover everything.
• One log feeds every tab, so you never type the same number twice.

━━━━━━━━━━
HOW IT WORKS
━━━━━━━━━━
1. Buy, then download the files from etsy.com (You › Purchases).
2. Open the quick-start guide. Use its Google Sheets link to make your own copy, or open the blank .xlsx in Excel.
3. Setup, about 5 minutes: pick your first month, then list your income, spending categories, goals, debts, accounts and bills.
4. Log each money move in Transactions. Amounts are always positive: the category decides if it's money in or money out.
5. Once a week: pick the month on the Dashboard, then type your bank balance in Accounts to see that everything matches.

FAQ
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Does it work in Excel?
No. It's made for Google Sheets (free with any Google account). The guided setup is built with Google Apps Script, which Excel, Numbers and Excel Online can't run. If you use Excel at work, that's fine: you just need a free Google account for this.

Can I use it on my phone?
Yes, for day-to-day use. Do the one-time setup on a computer (Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox; it takes about 10 minutes). After that, open the sheet in the free Google Sheets app and log purchases on the Quick Add tab, where every column has a dropdown. Both partners can do this from their own phones if you share the sheet with each other.

Is my data private?
Yes. When you click the link, you make your own copy in your own Google Drive. I can't see your copy or anything you type into it. The setup helper only has access to the one sheet it lives in (Google's "current spreadsheet only" permission). It doesn't touch your other files or your email. It only goes online for two things: the free U.S. government (NHTSA) VIN decoder, if you choose to look up a car, and the optional suggestion box, which sends only what you type there.

Google says "This app isn't verified." Is that safe?
Yes, that's normal for templates like this. The first time you click Let's get started, Google asks you to allow the setup helper. Because it's a small, private script inside your own copy, and not a big public app, Google shows this warning. Click Advanced, then Go to Couples Paycheck Budget (unsafe), then Allow. Can I get a refund? It's a digital item.
Because it's an instant digital download, I can't accept returns. But if something doesn't work, message me on Etsy and I'll make it right. Most setup problems are fixed in a couple of minutes (usually it's the two-Google-accounts issue below).

We each have a Google account. Which one do we use?
One of you makes the copy, then shares it with the other (Share button → their email → Editor). You'll both see the same budget. If the setup button does nothing or you see an "unable to open" error, you're probably signed into more than one Google account in the same browser. Open an incognito/private window, sign into just one account, and try again.

Do I get updates?
Yes. If I release an improved version, I'll update the download on Etsy, and you can download it again anytime from Your account → Purchases and reviews. I'll also send a message to past buyers when there's something worth switching for. Your current copy keeps working no matter what.

What do I need for "Ask Gemini"?
It's optional. The last setup screen gives you ready-to-copy prompts written from your own numbers. To use them inside Google Sheets, your Google account needs Gemini in Sheets (included in some paid Google plans, like Google AI plans or eligible Google Workspace plans). With a free account, you can paste the same prompt into the free Gemini app at gemini.google.com. The budget works fully without Gemini.

How long does setup take?
About 10 minutes. Typical amounts are already filled in, you can skip anything, and you can change any answer later with Edit my answers.

Is this financial advice?
No. It's a budgeting tool for personal use, not tax, legal or investment advice. Comparisons use published national averages from the Federal Reserve and the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Your situation may be different.

Set the paycheck period
Use Settings dates for the period you are planning, then enter planned paycheck income in B17.

Assign spending and savings
Enter category plans in B19:B38 and up to five savings allocations in E19:E23. Use nonnegative amounts, including zero for unused rows.

Check unassigned money

100 category allocation rows. 1000 income and expense rows. Automatic actual spending totals. Built for clear inputs and visual summaries.

GOOGLE SHEETS
Open the link in your guide, sign in to your own Google account and choose File > Make a copy. The shared master is view-only. Use your own private copy for real information.

MICROSOFT EXCEL
The XLSX opens in desktop Microsoft Excel. Excel software is not included.

WORKBOOK TABS
Summary, Records, Transactions.

PREPARED CAPACITY
Records: 101 prepared rows (98 initially blank, 3 examples); Transactions: 1001 prepared rows (998 initially blank, 3 examples). Example rows are excluded from Live summaries. Prepared formula ranges are fixed; extending the workbook requires updating formulas and validation.

HOW IT WORKS
1. Choose a month on Summary!D4. Enter the first day of the month.
2. On Records, add one category allocation per month. Use Live, a unique Reference ID and a nonnegative assigned budget.
3. On Transactions, enter received income as Income, then record spending as Expense. Expense category names and months must match allocations.
4. Actual used and remaining category budget calculate automatically. Savings transfers can use a Savings category consistently; avoid entering the same movement twice.
5. Income still unassigned is received income minus assigned budgets. Income less actual spending is a separate result. Missing income stays blank; an explicit zero Income entry is valid.

INPUTS AND EXAMPLES
Edit amber input cells. Use Live and a unique ID for real entries. Leave calculated cells intact. Blank or invalid required inputs and duplicate IDs are flagged; resolve them before relying on totals. All displayed example amounts, dates and guest details are fictional.

SCOPE
Manual cash-based budget planning. No bank imports, investment tracking or automatic account balances. Use one currency; display formats do not convert currencies.

CHECKED FORMAT
Representative calculations and input changes were checked in desktop Microsoft Excel 16.0 and native Google Sheets. Appearance can vary by application and screen.

LICENSE AND SUPPORT

This zero-based budget spreadsheet and standalone HTML app let you list your income, assign every dollar across your own categories, and log your real spending against that plan — with a live "Left to allocate" check that turns green the moment your budget hits exactly $0.

WHAT YOU CAN DO

• Explore fictional Sample Data in the standalone app without touching your own numbers.

YOUR DOWNLOAD
One ZIP, SortedSpender_ZeroBasedBudget.zip, containing exactly:
1. 15_Zero_Based_Budget.xlsx — 6-tab workbook: Read Me, Categories, Income, Budget Allocation, Transactions, Dashboard.
2. 15_Zero_Based_Budget.html — standalone app with Sample Data mode, independent of the spreadsheet.
3. 15_Buyer_Guide.pdf — four-page English setup and compatibility guide.

Extract the ZIP before opening the files. The images show fictional sample data. The buyer workbook and app both start with a few illustrative example rows, clearly marked, that you replace with your own. The app and spreadsheet keep independent records; they do not synchronize with each other.

HOW THE CALCULATIONS WORK
Categories is the single source of truth for category names — Budget Allocation mirrors it live, so renaming a category there updates everywhere else automatically. Budget Allocation's "Actual spent" column totals your Transactions by category with SUMIFS; a MATCH/IFERROR check flags any transaction whose category no longer matches your list instead of letting it vanish from your totals unnoticed. "Left to allocate" is simply your total income minus your total allocated amount — $0.00 means every dollar has a job.

COMPATIBILITY AND TESTING
The XLSX was reopened and recalculated with a spreadsheet engine, and every formula (SUMIFS, MATCH, IFERROR, REPT for the text progress bar) was checked against hand-computed expected values, including edge cases: an invalid/renamed category correctly flags "Check category," a zero-allocated category shows a blank percentage instead of a #DIV/0 error, and the "Left to allocate" conditional coloring switches correctly between $0 and non-$0 states. The standalone app's logic mirrors the workbook's math independently and was exercised end-to-end in an automated browser, including its Sample Data mode, add/remove row controls, backup export/import, reload persistence and print function.

This exact workbook — not a stand-in test file — was uploaded to Google Drive and opened in an interactive, signed-in Google Sheets session and checked tab by tab. Every dropdown (Category, Type), the SUMIFS/MATCH/IFERROR formulas, the coral/sage conditional coloring, and the text-based savings-goal progress bar all converted and displayed correctly. The one real limitation found: the Dashboard's "Allocated vs. actual" bar chart does not survive Google Drive's conversion to its Sheets rendering engine — the chart's axis appears with no bars. This does not affect any number: the same figures the chart illustrates are already in the Budget Allocation table right next to it, and a buyer who wants a chart in Sheets can rebuild one with Insert > Chart in about 10 seconds (steps in the buyer guide and the Read Me tab).

GOOD TO KNOW
Digital download only; no physical product. USD only; no currency conversion. This is a manual planner — no bank connection, no automatic transaction import, no real-time balance sync. results.title: Zero Based Budget Spreadsheet for Google Sheets and Excel | Monthly Budget Planner, Dark Mode, Bill Tracker, Debt Payoff, Annual Dashboard
results.description:
▸ See it working before you buy: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1sqBG94-Tx6fSIHhQaTE8gavMlt0Nsp1-e4sIgRdQNCI/edit?usp=sharing

GIVE EVERY UNIT OF MONEY A JOB

A normal budget asks what is left at the end of the month. A zero-based budget asks, at the start, what every unit of money is for - rent, groceries, the car service in October, the part you refuse to touch.

The month is planned when LEFT TO ASSIGN reads zero. Not because you spent everything, but because nothing is still waiting for a decision. Money you assign to savings is assigned, not left over - which is why this file has no "left over" row at all. It has one row that has to reach zero, and a colour that tells you the moment it does: amber while money still has no job, red if you promised more than the month holds, green when the month is planned.

WHAT IS INSIDE

• Two .xlsx files - dark and light, identical in every formula
• ZERO-BASED PLAN - 12 monthly columns x 24 categories you can rename
• MONTH VIEW - pick a month and see, per category, what you assigned, how much the bills take, what you have logged and what is still free to spend
• BILLS - 30 recurring bills, sorted into the categories they belong to
• EXPENSES LOG - 500 rows, date, category, amount, with dropdowns
• DEBTS - 15 debts, months left and the month you become debt free, calculated
• SAVINGS - 10 goals with progress bars and what to put aside each month
• DASHBOARD - plan against reality month by month, three charts, top five categories
• START-HERE guide, five pages, plain English
• CATEGORIES - rename anything and every dropdown and plan row follows

THE PART THAT DOES THE WORK

Bills come out of their category on their own. You assign 620 to Housing, the rent is 620, and MONTH VIEW shows 0 still there - not 620. The number you read is what is actually free to spend, not what is left before the rent. That one detail is the difference between a budget you trust and a budget you argue with.

WORKS WHERE YOU WORK

Google Sheets and Excel 2016 or newer, Mac and Windows, and on the phone apps. Native formulas only - no macros, no add-ons, no security warning to click through. Nothing is sent anywhere: it is a file, and it sits where you keep it.

INSTANT DOWNLOAD

The zip contains both .xlsx files, the START-HERE guide, ready-made Google Sheets copy links and the licence. For personal use.

-----

IN ITALIANO

Un budget normale chiede che cosa resta a fine mese. Un budget a base zero chiede, all'inizio, a che cosa serve ogni euro: affitto, spesa, il tagliando di ottobre, la parte che non si tocca.

Il mese e' pianificato quando la riga LEFT TO ASSIGN segna zero. Non perche' hai speso tutto, ma perche' niente e' piu' in attesa di una decisione. I soldi che assegni al risparmio sono assegnati, non avanzati - per questo il file non ha nessuna riga "avanzo": ha una riga che deve arrivare a zero, e un colore che te lo dice.

results.title: Zero Based Budget Spreadsheet, Monthly Budget Planner, Paycheck Budget Bill Tracker, Budget by Paycheck Template, Instant Download XLSX
results.description:
A monthly budget workbook that does the one thing a generic budget template does not: it
proves, live, that every dollar has a job. Income minus every allocated dollar sits in one
cell at the top of the Budget tab, and that cell moves the instant you change any planned
amount.

THREE CLAIMS YOU CAN CHECK BEFORE YOU BUY

1. The zero-based proof is live: change any planned cell and the unallocated remainder
moves with it - and the same identity is verified to the cent by an independent
recomputation. The remainder is a formula, income minus the four group subtotals, not a
number anyone typed. A second implementation of the whole model - written in plain Python
from the specification rather than read back out of the file - is driven against twelve
seeded 80-transaction scenarios and has to agree on the identity, every category roll-up,
every group subtotal, every paycheck remainder and all eighteen data checks. 2,664
comparisons, zero disagreements.

2. It refuses to print a comfortable zero. When total income is zero or blank, the
remainder cell shows #N/A instead of $0.00 - because a zero remainder with no income
behind it is indistinguishable from a perfectly balanced month. That is the one wrong
answer that looks exactly like the right one, and this file will not print it.

3. Every bill is assigned to a specific paycheck. Four paychecks across the top, thirty
bill rows below, each carrying a validated 1-4 dropdown. Each check shows what it pays
minus the bills you hung on it, so an overloaded check is visible BEFORE the month starts
rather than on the day it bounces. A bill with an amount and no paycheck number prints NOT
ASSIGNED rather than quietly vanishing from every total.

WHAT IS INSIDE - NINE TABS

Start Here - the five minutes that set it up, in order.

Settings - the budget month and year, up to four income sources with a per-month amount
and a pay-frequency label, a live month label, and the three questions this file will not
answer for you.

Budget - 30 category rows in four groups (fixed costs, variable and everyday, savings and
goals, debt payoff). Planned is the only column you type. Actual fills itself from the
Spending Log. Difference and a status word on every row: NOT USED, UNPLANNED SPENDING,
REVIEW - OVER 2x PLANNED, OVER PLAN, EXACTLY ON PLAN or UNDER PLAN - never blank, never a
guess. The zero-based proof band sits above it all.

Paycheck Planner - four paychecks with a label and an amount, thirty bill rows each
assigned to one of them, and per-check income, assigned bills and remainder.

Spending Log - 150 rows. The category dropdown is built from the Budget tab's own category
cells, so the two lists cannot drift apart. Two guard columns on every row: whether the
date falls inside the budget month, and whether the category actually reaches a budget row.

Bills Checklist - 30 recurring bills with a due day, an amount and a Paid? dropdown, and a
still-due total that counts only what you have not ticked off.

Dashboard - planned against actual for all four groups with a bar chart, the month label,
the zero-based state, and the five categories furthest over plan, ranked live rather than
typed.

Data Checks - eighteen checks that read the live file, each with a plain-English line
saying what it means right now. Two of them are red the moment you open the file.

README - how it is built, what is locked, and what it will not do.

THREE ANSWER CELLS SHIP BLANK ON PURPOSE

The Settings tab asks you three questions and refuses to answer any of them: whether the
income you entered is take-home or gross, whether your savings goals are already Budget
rows, and whether all four paychecks land inside this month. Each verdict cell shows #N/A
until you pick Yes or No.

Budgeting gross pay as though it were take-home is the most common way a plan fails, and
it is invisible while it happens - the file has no way to tell the two apart from the
number alone, so it declines to assume. Every branching chain in the workbook ends in #N/A
rather than a plausible-looking default, because a wrong number that looks right is worse
than no number. Those three cells, plus the spare fourth income row, are the only input
cells outside the entry grids that ship empty.

THE PLANNED AMOUNTS ARE STARTING POINTS

Everything marked [SAMPLE] is there so you can watch the machinery work before you trust
it with your own numbers. The planned amounts that ship in the file are editable starting
points you are meant to replace. None of them is a recommendation, a rule of thumb, or a
percentage anyone should copy. There is no budgeting formula built into this workbook on
purpose: the only rule it enforces is that your own numbers add up.

EIGHTEEN DATA CHECKS, EVERY ONE OF THEM PROVEN TO FIRE

A guard that has never been shown to fire is a comment, not a guard. Every one of the
eighteen checks has a scenario in the verify suite that pastes the exact bad data it
exists for - bypassing the dropdowns the way a real paste does - recalculates the whole
model and asserts the check goes red, and asserts it was green before the paste so the
paste is what moved it. 20 scenarios, 85 assertions, zero failures.

WHAT IS LOCKED

Seven of the nine tabs carry passwordless sheet protection so a stray keystroke cannot
wipe a formula: Start Here, Settings, Budget, Paycheck Planner, Dashboard, Data Checks and
README. Every amber input cell on those tabs is unlocked and typable, and no formula cell
on them is left unlocked. The Spending Log and the Bills Checklist ship completely
unprotected so you can sort, filter and insert rows. There is no password anywhere.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO

It does not connect to a bank, import a statement, or read a card feed - every figure in
it is one you typed or one it computed from what you typed. It plans ONE month; a new
month is a new copy of the file. It does not compute tax, interest, a debt payoff
schedule, an amortisation table, or an investment return. It does not track account
balances or net worth. It handles four paychecks, not five - and the Settings question
about paychecks landing inside the month exists to make you notice when that matters. It
does not tell you what to spend: there is no recommended percentage anywhere in the file,
because there is no percentage that is right for everyone. It is not a shared or
multi-user tool.

FORMAT

A standard .xlsx workbook plus two PDFs. No macros, no add-ons, no external links, no
named ranges, no XLOOKUP, no dynamic arrays. Every range is explicitly bounded. This file
was built and recalculated in LibreOffice Calc; no claim is made here about how any other
application behaves, because a claim nobody has tested is a wish.

The two guides are the same ten pages in US Letter and A4, with the same section on the
same page number in both.

This workbook is a planning and tracking tool. It is not financial advice and it makes no
recommendation about how anyone should allocate money. Figures you rely on should be
confirmed with a licensed professional where relevant. This is an independent product and
is not affiliated with or endorsed by any bank, employer, payroll provider or financial
institution.

This template was created using AI tools that I directed and reviewed.

The zero-based budget method works because it forces you to be intentional about every dollar before the month starts. This spreadsheet is built to support that process — showing you your income at the top, subtracting every category of spending, and keeping a live running balance so you always know exactly how much is left to assign.

⚖️ WHAT IS ZERO-BASED BUDGETING?
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Zero-based budgeting is a method in which every available amount of income is assigned to a specific purpose at the beginning of the month.

The basic structure is:

INCOME − EXPENSES − SAVINGS − DEBT PAYMENTS = ZERO

A zero balance does not mean that every amount must be spent.

It means your income has been intentionally allocated toward bills, daily expenses, savings, investments, debt repayment, or other financial priorities.

⚖️ WHAT IS ZERO-BASED BUDGETING?
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Zero-based budgeting assigns every available amount to a specific category.

The basic structure is:

INCOME − EXPENSES − SAVINGS − DEBT PAYMENTS = ZERO

A zero balance does not mean every amount must be spent.

It means your available income has been intentionally assigned toward needs, lifestyle spending, savings, sinking funds, debt payments, or other financial goals.

results.title: Zero Based Budget Spreadsheet, Google Sheets & Excel Budget Planner, Paycheck Expense Tracker, Give Every Dollar a Job, YNAB Alternative
results.description:
Give every dollar a job before the month begins. This zero based budget spreadsheet for Google Sheets and Excel is the YNAB-style money system where you assign every dollar of income to a category until the number that matters most, To Be Budgeted, hits exactly $0. No more "where did it all go" at the end of the month. Every dollar already has a place, and you can see it.

Most budget templates either plan or track. This one does both, in one tool, so the plan you make is the plan you actually live.


GIVE EVERY DOLLAR A JOB UNTIL YOU REACH $0
The Budget tab is the zero-based grid: your income at the top, then 10 expense groups with automatic subtotals, and the signature TO BE BUDGETED row underneath. You assign income across the groups until that row reads $0, with a per-month status strip that tells you at a glance whether you are over, under, or perfectly balanced. In the example, the Rivera household assigns all $87,600 of annual income, so To Be Budgeted lands on $0 and every dollar is working.


PLAN IT, THEN ACTUALLY TRACK IT
The Transactions tab is your real-life log: enter a date, pick a category from the dropdown, type the amount, and the month fills in on its own. Sample rows show you how it works, and pre-formatted blank rows are ready for your own spending. This is the half most budgets skip. Here, your plan and your actual money live side by side, so you always know if you are still on track.


SEE YOUR FINANCIAL HEALTH IN PLAIN ENGLISH
The Insights tab reads your numbers back to you like a calm, organized friend who is good with money. Four KPI tiles up top, then a financial-health check shown as simple glyph chips: your housing ratio, your savings rate against the common 15% target, your debt load, and a check that your budget actually zeroes out. A "Where your money goes" bar breakdown shows each group at a glance. In the example, that reads as a 16% savings rate, 34% to housing, 6% to debt, and $14,400 going to savings across the year.


WHAT IS INCLUDED
- A Google Sheets "make a copy" link, yours to copy and keep forever.
- An .xlsx file for Microsoft Excel, same tool, same formulas.
- A blank-starter version so you can begin completely fresh, plus a fully filled-in example so you can see exactly how everything works.
- A PDF quick-start guide that has you set up in a couple of minutes.
- 5 tabs: Start Here, Budget, Transactions, Insights, and Setup.
- Light and dark themes, both included.


WHY IT FEELS DIFFERENT
- Every formula tested. We verify each formula computes correctly before it ships. No broken cells, no math that quietly drifts.
- Fully unlocked. Edit every cell, color, and formula. Nothing is protected. It is yours.
- Works in Google Sheets and Excel. Build wherever you already are.
- Real example numbers, never lorem ipsum. You see a real budget working, then make it your own.
- A real model, not a static grid. Enter your numbers and the To Be Budgeted row, the group subtotals, and the Insights health checks figure themselves out, so you can see at a glance whether every dollar is assigned and where you stand.


HOW DELIVERY WORKS
This is an instant digital download. The moment your payment clears, Etsy gives you the files plus your "make a copy" Google Sheets link. Open the PDF quick-start guide first, it walks you through making your own copy and opening the Excel file, step by step.


100% DIGITAL, NOTHING SHIPS
There is no physical item and nothing will be mailed to you. You receive digital files and a Google Sheets link instantly after purchase, ready to use on your computer, tablet, or phone.


HOW TO MAKE IT YOURS
Open the Start Here tab, follow the three quick steps, then type your real income and categories over the example until To Be Budgeted reads $0. Log your spending on the Transactions tab as the month goes. The blank-starter version is there if you would rather begin from scratch. Change the colors, rename the categories, add your own, it all keeps working. If you ever get stuck, we are one message away.

results.title: Zero Based Budget Spreadsheet, Give Every Dollar a Job (Google Sheets & Excel)
results.description:
A zero-based budget spreadsheet for Google Sheets and Excel. Type what each category gets, and one number tells you when every dollar has a job.

Give every dollar a job. Assign what comes in until there is nothing left, and this tab tells you when you are done.

Four tabs, one workbook. On Setup, name your categories, with In or Out and a group, and set the budget year. On Assign, pick the month, choose whether to assign from what you plan to come in or what actually came in, type last month's leftover if there is one, then type what each category gets. Left to assign updates as you type, and the line under it reads All assigned, in green, when it reaches zero. Log what you spend on Quick Add, a row each time, and Assign shows Spent and Left beside every category for the month you picked.

What it does for you

- One number that tells you when you are done. To assign is your income for the month plus anything left over from last month. Left to assign is what is still not given to a category, in one figure at the top of the tab. At zero it reads All assigned, in green. While some money still has no job it shows the amount left to assign. If you have given out more than you have, it says so, in red.
- The plan is typed where you read it. What each category gets is typed on Assign, in the Assigned column, and Setup's Assigned column shows the same figure back to you. There is one place to type a plan, so two plans can never disagree.
- Assign from what you expect, or from what landed. Assign from is a dropdown with two settings. What you plan to come in uses the amounts on your income rows. What actually came in uses the money logged as In on Quick Add for the month showing, so in a month with a bonus, or a short one, the extra or the gap shows up in Left to assign.
- Last month's leftover comes in as income. Left over from last month is a cell at the top of Assign. Type what was left at the end of last month and it is added to what you have to assign this month. Leave it empty in your first month.
- Where it goes, category by category. Under the summary, every category from Setup with its In / Out, its Group, what you Assigned, what you Spent in the month showing, and what is Left. A category that has gone past what it was given reads red. A totals row shows Assigned to go out this month beside what actually went out.
- One category list, one log. Categories live on Setup, with room for 36, and a name you change there carries to Assign and to the Quick Add dropdown. Spending is typed once, on Quick Add, and Assign reads it. Pick a different month at the top of Assign and Spent, Left and the Quick Add totals follow it.
- A note when something is off. If a Quick Add row uses a category that isn't on Setup, a line at the foot of Assign counts them. If two Setup rows share a name, Setup says so. If a Quick Add row has no usable date, Quick Add says so.
- Hard to break by accident. Colored cells are yours to type in, and empty ones glow until you fill them. Everything else is locked so the numbers keep working.
- Four color themes in one file. Shore, Meadow, Slate and Midnight, switched from a dropdown on Start Here. All four tabs recolor. There is nothing to choose at checkout.
- Works on your phone. A Quick Add row is a date, what it was, a category from a dropdown, and an amount.

What's in the download

- Sortment Zero-Based Budget.xlsx, filled with an example so you can see it working: a household's month with every dollar assigned, Left to assign reading All assigned, and one category that ran past what it was given.
- Sortment Zero-Based Budget - blank.xlsx, the same four tabs, empty, for your own numbers.
- A quick-start PDF with the two Google Sheets links (example and blank). Open one, choose File > Make a copy, and it's yours.

The four tabs

- Start Here: how it works, and where to pick your theme
- Setup: the budget year, and room for 36 categories, each with In or Out and a group. Its Assigned column shows what you typed on Assign
- Assign: pick the month, choose what to assign from, type last month's leftover and what each category gets, and read Left to assign. Under it, every category with Assigned, Spent and Left
- Quick Add: log what you spend, on your phone or your laptop. 600 rows, and the only place spending is typed

How it works

1. Name your categories on Setup, with In or Out and a group. Your income is a category marked In. Set the budget year at the top.
2. Open Assign. Pick the month, choose Assign from, and type last month's leftover if you have one. Then type what comes in on your income rows and what each spending category gets, and watch Left to assign fall.
3. Keep going until it reads All assigned. If it says you have assigned more than you have, take some back off a category.
4. Log what you spend on Quick Add: a date, what it was, a category, and an amount. Assign shows Spent and Left beside each category for the month you picked. A new month is a new pick.

Compatibility

- Google Sheets and Excel. Use whichever you prefer, or both.
- One purchase, no subscription. Nothing to install, no add-ons, no monthly fee, no bank connection. You type your categories, your plan and what you spend, and the workbook does the rest.
- Phone, tablet, laptop. Day to day, the Google Sheets or Excel app on your phone is enough to log a row on Quick Add and read Assign. Do the first setup on something bigger if you can.
- The font is Montserrat, which is free. Install it for the exact look in Excel, or skip it. Everything works without it.
- It comes in dollars. Changing the currency is ordinary cell formatting, and the quick-start shows where.

Questions

Is this a physical item?
No. It's a digital download: two Excel files, a PDF quick-start, and links to copy the Google Sheets versions. Nothing is mailed.

Do I make a new plan every month?
The amounts you assign are one plan, and they stay put when you change the month. What follows the month is Spent, Left, the Quick Add totals and, on the What actually came in setting, Income this month. If your income and categories are much the same from month to month, pick the month and log what you spend. If a month is different, change the amounts. The previous month's amounts are not kept, so save a copy first if you want to look back at them.

Does what's left in a category carry into next month?
No. A category's Left is Assigned less Spent for the month showing, and it starts again from the assigned amount in the next month. What carries forward is one figure, Left over from last month, at the top of Assign. You type it, and it is added to what you have to assign.

Where do I type my income?
Your income is a category on Setup marked In, and there is room for more than one. On Assign, type what comes in on those rows and it becomes Income this month. Switch Assign from to What actually came in and the tab uses the In rows logged on Quick Add for the month instead.

Does it tell me what to give each category?
No. Left to assign is a figure, and where the money goes is your call. There is no rule of thumb in it.

Does it connect to my bank, or remind me about anything?
No. You log spending yourself, a few seconds a row. It can't send a reminder. That's the trade: nothing to connect, nothing to pay monthly, and you always know what is still left to assign.

Does it have a dashboard, debt payoff or sinking funds?
No. This is the Assign tab, a category list and a spending log. If you want the whole month on one screen with those tabs as well, that's the Sortment Budget Planner. Debt payoff on its own is the Sortment Debt Payoff, and funds on their own are the Sortment Sinking Funds.

Is this the Sortment Budget Planner with tabs taken out?
Close, and one tab is different. Same Setup, same Quick Add, same Start Here, and the same way of working. Where the Budget Planner has a Dashboard, a Monthly tab, Sinking Funds, Debt Payoff and an Annual view, this has Assign. The Monthly tab reports on a plan typed on Setup and shows what is left of it. Assign is where the plan is typed, working down from what comes in, and it shows what is left to plan. If your way is to give every dollar a job, this is the one to get.

How many categories and rows?
36 categories and 600 Quick Add rows. When Quick Add fills, save a copy for the year you finished and clear it with Clear_QuickAdd from the name box. Clear_Assign clears the amounts on Assign the same way. The quick-start shows where.

Do I get Google Sheets or Excel?
Both. Same workbook, same four tabs, same four themes. For Google Sheets, use the Make a copy link in your quick-start guide. An Excel file you upload to Google Drive yourself works, but loses the protection that warns you before you type over a formula.

Do I pick a theme at checkout?
No. All four themes are in the one file. Pick one on Start Here and change it any time.

What if I type over something I shouldn't?
Undo puts it back. The cells that do the work are locked, so it's hard to do by accident. For a clean start, open the blank file or make a fresh copy from the Google Sheets link.

License and support

Sortment Zero-Based Budget is licensed for your personal use. Please don't share, resell, or repost the files. If a friend wants one, point them to the shop.

Because this is a digital file, Etsy doesn't allow returns once it's downloaded. If something isn't working the way you expect, message me on Etsy with what's happening (a screenshot helps) and I'll help you get it sorted. I usually reply within one business day.

Sortment. Everything, sorted.

Zero-Based Budgeting Spreadsheet Template in Excel and Google Sheets

What is Zero-Based Budgeting?

Zero-Based Budgeting is a budgeting method where you allocate every dollar of your income to a specific purpose at the start of the month. Unlike traditional budgeting, which may carry over balances, Zero-Based Budgeting begins with a “zero balance.” This approach ensures that every penny is assigned to cover your expenses, savings, or investments, giving you full control over your financial life.

Who Can Benefit From This Template?

– Individuals Seeking Financial Clarity
If you want to know exactly where every dollar is going and ensure your spending aligns with your goals, this template is the perfect tool for you.

– Families & Households
Effectively manage household finances by allocating your income across necessary categories with ease, keeping everything organized.

– Business Owners & Freelancers
Track both personal and business-related expenses, helping you separate and manage your finances efficiently.

Key Benefits of Zero-Based Budgeting

– Complete Control Over Your Finances
You assign every dollar, ensuring that your income is spent or saved purposefully, whether it’s for bills, debt repayment, or investments.

– Improved Financial Awareness
Regularly reviewing your income and expenses gives you insight into your financial habits, allowing you to make smarter, more informed decisions.

– Accelerated Debt Repayment
Allocate extra funds toward paying off debt, helping you clear obligations faster and achieve your financial goals more efficiently.

– Increased Savings & Investment Potential
By scrutinizing your budget, you can identify areas to cut back, freeing up more money for savings and investments to build long-term wealth.

Why You Need This Template

– Fully Customizable
Tailor the template to your needs by choosing your year, month, and currency (dollars, euros, etc.), ensuring it fits your specific financial situation.

– Clear Categorization
Organize your budget into categories like income, bills, savings, expenses, debts, and investments, making it easy to track and manage your finances.

– Monthly Budget Planning
Allocate a set amount to each category at the start of the month, helping you avoid overspending and stay within your financial limits.

– Automated Tracking
The template tracks your income and expenses automatically, providing real-time updates and keeping you informed about your financial status.

– Efficient Debt & Bill Management
Set up reminders for bill payments and track your debt repayment progress, ensuring that no payment is missed and helping you stay on top of your financial responsibilities.

How It Works

1. Set Your Budget
At the beginning of each month, input your total income and allocate it across various categories such as bills, savings, expenses, investments, and debt repayment.

• Fixed Expenses and Variable Expenses: your spending plan, by category
• Sinking Funds: how much to set aside each paycheck and each month to reach a goal by its date; a due date that has passed turns red
• Debts: Avalanche (highest APR first) or Snowball (smallest balance first) pay order, with estimated months to payoff and interest for each debt at its current payment. Type 0 when a debt is paid off and it leaves the pay order
• Transactions: a 1,000-row log (about 83 a month). Type or paste from your bank; a Check column flags any row that won't count
• Lists: rename categories here; any plan row or transaction still using an old name is flagged so you can re-pick it

HOW IT WORKS
1. Download and unzip the files. Open the blank workbook in Google Sheets (upload the .xlsx to Google Drive, then File > Save as Google Sheets), in Excel 2016 or later, or in LibreOffice.
2. Follow the 6 steps on the Start Here tab. It takes about 10 minutes.
3. Log or paste your transactions, then check the Monthly tab once a month.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Formulas are locked (no password) in Excel and LibreOffice. Google Sheets doesn't keep those locks when it converts the file; to protect them there, use Data > Protect sheets and ranges > Show a warning
• No macros and no add-ons
• Debt estimates are per debt at its own payment; the money freed up when a debt is paid off (the snowball roll-over) isn't added in
• Made for household budgets, not business bookkeeping
• Digital download only; nothing is shipped

HOW IT WAS MADE
Designed by GF Interactive. The spreadsheet formulas, app code and preview images were built with AI assistance and checked by hand; the formulas were also checked by full recalculation and against an independent calculation of the sample numbers.

Refund on request within 30 days, no proof required.

Educational budgeting tool with example figures. Not financial, tax or legal advice. Sample data is fictional. No savings, debt-payoff or other results are promised; payoff months and interest are estimates. Not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Google, Microsoft or The Document Foundation; the names only identify the apps the workbook opens in.

FAQ

Does it work in Google Sheets?
Yes. Unzip the download, upload the .xlsx to Google Drive, open it with Google Sheets, then choose File > Save as Google Sheets. Google Sheets doesn't keep the formula locks from the file; to add your own, use Data > Protect sheets and ranges > Show a warning.

Which versions of Excel?
Microsoft Excel 2016 or later, or Microsoft 365. The workbook uses no functions newer than Excel 2016 and no macros. It also opens in LibreOffice.

Is it envelope budgeting or zero-based budgeting?
Both. Each category on the Monthly tab works as an envelope (budget, spent, what's left), and the zero-based check shows whether your plan accounts for every dollar of income.

Do I have to connect my bank?
No. Nothing connects to your bank. You type or paste your transactions.

Is my data private?
The workbook is a file you keep. The bonus tracker app saves what you type only in your own browser and doesn't connect to the internet.

I get paid weekly (or every other week). Does it fit?
Yes. Set paychecks per year on Start Here (52, 26, 24 or 12) and each income line can have its own frequency.

The due date turns red once it has passed. When fewer paychecks than one month's worth are left, the monthly set-aside shows the full amount still needed, so your plan stays realistic.

Can I change the categories?
Yes. Rename them on the Lists tab. Any plan row or transaction still using the old name is flagged by its Check column so you can re-pick it.

Does the debt payoff include the snowball roll-over?
The Debts tab gives you the pay order (Avalanche or Snowball) and estimates months and interest for each debt at its own payment. When a debt is paid off, type 0 as its balance and move its payment to the new Pay order #1 yourself.

How many transactions does it hold?
The log has 1,000 rows, about 83 a month.

Does the tracker app work on my phone?
It's made for Chrome or Edge on a computer. Many phones can't open a downloaded HTML file in a browser, so phone use isn't promised. The workbook itself is the main product.

No. It's built for household budgets. Selling online too? Our Seller Bookkeeping Sheet tracks shop sales and fees: https://www.etsy.com/listing/4593364947

No. It's an organizing tool with example figures. You make your own decisions.

3. Debts — 15 rows: name, type (credit card, student loan, car loan, personal loan, medical, mortgage, other), current balance, APR %, minimum payment and an optional custom priority, with a Status check on every row

• A Status column checks every debt: a missing balance, APR or minimum payment is flagged and the row is left out instead of being quietly counted as zero

WHAT YOU SEE WHEN YOU OPEN IT
The first tab is START HERE. Three steps, on one page:
1. At the top of YOUR DEBTS, pick how to pay them off, type any extra money each month, and the first month of your plan.
2. One line for each card or loan. Five boxes: the debt's name, card or loan, what you owe, the interest rate (APR) and the minimum payment. Your latest statement has the numbers.
3. Open YOUR PLAN to see what to pay each debt, month by month. Each time you pay, type it on YOUR PAYMENTS.
Beside it is EXAMPLE (filled in) - a finished plan with four debts: a store card, a Visa, a car loan and a 0% family loan, with 200 a month extra. Look at it, change it, and see what finished looks like. It never touches your own pages.
The figures in the pictures are an example household, so you can see a full plan. Your own pages open empty and fill in as you type.

WHAT IT WORKS OUT FOR YOU
YOUR PLAN - what to pay each debt, every month. At the top: the month you are debt free, the interest in total (an estimate), what you have paid so far and what you still owe.
YOUR DEBTS - for each debt: paid so far, owed now, the month it is paid off, and its interest in total.
Two charts: what you owe, month by month, and paid so far against owed now, for each debt.

THE PAYMENTS YOU REALLY MAKE
Type each payment on YOUR PAYMENTS: the date, which debt, and how much. Room for 500 payment lines.
Still using a card? Pick Yes under Still using this card? and type about how much you spend on it a month. The sheet adds that to the card each month.

HOW THE INTEREST IS WORKED OUT
Cards: day by day, on what was owed at the end of the month before. Loans: one month of interest each month.
A 0% debt? Type 0.
It is an estimate. Your lender's figure may differ, because it also depends on the day you pay.

IF A LINE WILL NOT COUNT, IT SAYS SO
Every debt line and every payment line has a Check box. If something on a line will not count, it says so in words, on that line. Three of the messages, word for word from the file:

"CHECK THIS: this line does not say Credit card or Loan, so it is not in your plan. Click the box and pick one."
"CHECK THIS: there is no date, so it is not counted. Type it as year-month-day, like 2026-03-14."

There is no budget page and no link to your bank.

Three charts, your first 10 debts in payoff order with progress bars (all 20 are on the Progress sheet), the next payments due and a plan at a glance
• Payment Log with 600 rows and a counter that shows how many are left: add the date, the debt and the amount. The balance after each payment is worked out for you, with the interest since your last payment estimated by the day. Type the balance from your statement any time to keep it exact

results.title: Debt Payoff Tracker Spreadsheet, Google Sheets Snowball and Avalanche Calculator
results.description:
Snowball or avalanche? This spreadsheet shows you both, side by side, and tells you what the difference costs.

Snowball pays the smallest balance first, so you usually clear your first debt sooner and it feels like progress. Avalanche pays the highest interest rate first, so you usually pay less interest in total. Neither is wrong. But you should be able to see the number before you choose.

WHAT YOU GET
One .xlsx spreadsheet file with six connected tabs. Formulas only: no macros, no add-ons, no subscription.

PERFECT FOR
- Anyone carrying more than one balance and unsure which to attack
- Credit card, store card, car loan and student loan payoff
- Couples getting every debt onto one page for the first time
- Anyone following a debt-free plan and wanting the real interest number
- Anyone who has been told to pick a method and wants to see why

WHAT IS INSIDE
Debts. One row per debt: balance, APR and minimum payment. The sheet ranks them both ways automatically, so you never have to sort anything, works out how many months each would take at the minimum alone, and keeps a running remaining balance as you log payments. If a minimum payment does not even cover the interest, it says so in plain words instead of showing an impossible number. For an interest-free debt, type 0 as the APR or leave it blank: both count as 0%.

Compare. The answer first: how many months each method takes, the total interest each one costs you, and the difference between them in dollars. Then both payoff orders, with every debt listed. Change the extra payment and watch both numbers move.

Payments. Log each payment and split it between interest and principal.

Dashboard. Starting debt, principal cleared, still owed, percent done, debts still open and total interest paid. That last number is on the page deliberately. It is money that bought you nothing. Below it: months to debt-free and the interest still ahead on the avalanche plan. Both count from what you owe now, so they fall as you log payments.

Payoff Math. The month-by-month working behind the comparison. You never need to open it.

Start Here. Plain-English setup, one page.

Holds 40 debts and 996 payments. The comparison includes every debt you enter.

HOW THE COMPARISON COUNTS
It works month by month from what you owe now: each starting balance minus the principal you have logged. It assumes you pay the same total every month (all minimums plus your extra), interest is charged monthly at APR / 12, and each cleared payment rolls into the next debt in the order. It runs for up to 30 years. If your debts would take longer at your payment, it says so instead of showing a number. Your lender's own figures can differ, for example because of fees, rate changes or daily interest.

WHAT FILE YOU GET
One .xlsx spreadsheet. The formulas were checked by recalculating them in LibreOffice Calc on the made-up example data shown in the photos. Tested in Google Sheets: every formula recalculated by Google with zero errors. Built to open in Excel with no macros, not yet tested in Excel.

results.title: Procurement Savings Tracker Spreadsheet, Supplier Cost Savings Log, Negotiation Savings Report, Purchasing Dashboard, Excel & Google Sheets
results.description:
Prove what your purchasing team saved, and show exactly where it came from. This procurement savings tracker records every negotiated saving - baseline cost, negotiated cost, annual volume, savings type, supplier, project and status - and works out annual and realized savings for your leadership report.

WHY YOU'LL LIKE IT
- Enter the baseline unit cost, the negotiated unit cost and the annual volume. The tracker calculates unit savings, annual savings, savings rate and baseline spend for you.
- Realized savings to date are counted from each initiative's effective date, so you report what has been earned so far, not just what was promised.
- Every initiative is tagged Hard or Soft savings, so finance and leadership see cost reduction and cost avoidance separately.
- A Finance Verified flag shows how much of your realized savings finance has confirmed.
- Supplier View and Project View rank savings from largest to smallest on their own. There is nothing to sort or type.
- The Dashboard shows 8 KPI cards, progress to your annual savings target, and savings by status, supplier, savings type and category, with a chart for status and one for your top 8 suppliers.
- Pipeline view by status (Identified, Negotiating, Contracted, Implemented, Cancelled), with a Counts as setting that decides which statuses count toward your totals.
- A data check flags any type, status or category that is not on your Settings lists, so a typo does not hide savings from the totals.

WHAT'S INCLUDED (one Excel file, 7 tabs)
Cover, Read Me, Settings, Savings Log, Supplier View, Project View and Dashboard. The Savings Log has room for 200 initiatives (and the ranked views list up to 30 suppliers and 30 projects) and comes with 31 sample rows so you can see how it works. The Read Me has step-by-step instructions and a glossary.

HOW IT WORKS
1. On Settings, enter your as-of date (or clear it to use today's date), your annual savings target and a period label.
2. Rename the categories, savings types and statuses to match how your team talks.
3. Replace the sample rows in the Savings Log with your own initiatives.
4. Update each status as the work moves from Identified to Negotiating, Contracted and Implemented.
5. Open the Dashboard for the numbers to share with leadership.

WORKS WITH
Excel and Google Sheets. No macros, add-ins or subscription needed. In Google Sheets, choose File > Import > Upload and pick the file.

INSTANT DOWNLOAD
Your file is available to download as soon as your payment clears. Nothing is shipped.

GOOD TO KNOW
All names and figures in the sample data are made up for demonstration. The tracker is a planning and reporting tool and does not give accounting, tax or financial advice. It does not promise any particular savings result. For personal use and use within your own business; please do not resell or share the file.

results.title: Savings Tracker Spreadsheet | Sinking Funds Tracker, Savings Goal Planner, Emergency Fund, Deposit and Withdrawal Log (Excel, Google Sheets)
results.description:
The car insurance renews in six weeks, the holiday gifts come in December, and the water heater will pick its own moment. You put a little aside for each of them, but it all sits in one savings account, and the balance alone does not tell you whether the insurance money will be there on the day the bill arrives.

This workbook gives every savings pot its own row: an emergency fund, a sinking fund for a bill that comes back every year, a savings goal with a date. You type the target, the date you need it by and what is in it today, and from then on you log every deposit and withdrawal. It then works out what each fund has saved, what is still missing, how many months are left and what it needs each month to be ready before its date, and it says in plain words which fund is on track, which one is close to its date and which one has fallen behind.

You also type what you plan to put in each month, so the workbook can tell you when the plan is not enough: the fund turns amber and shows how much it is short per month.

Built for households that save in pots - emergency fund, car insurance, property tax, holidays, back to school, a trip. This is a spreadsheet you fill in yourself - it does not connect to your bank, and it does not work out interest: when your account pays interest, you log it as money in. Works in both Excel and Google Sheets. No subscription.

WHAT YOU GET

- FUNDS tab - one row per fund, with room for 30: name, type, target amount, target date, starting balance, planned per month and Done? - plus saved, still to save, percent full, months left, needed per month, how far the plan falls short, put in this month and a plain-words status
- TRANSACTIONS tab - every deposit and withdrawal, with room for 1500: date, fund, in, out and notes - plus a flag when a row needs fixing
- MONTHLY tab - twelve months side by side: put in, taken out, net saved and a running total, plus what went into and out of each fund each month
- DASHBOARD - twelve numbers that update themselves: total saved, the total of your targets, how much of them is saved, what your funds need this month, what you plan to put in, how far the plan falls short, put in and taken out this month, funds to act on, funds to watch, funds at target and rows to fix - plus a plain-words status line and a table by fund type
- SETUP tab - two settings: how many days before a target date a fund turns amber (60 days to start), and which twelve months MONTHLY shows
- LISTS tab - the dropdown words: three fund types (savings goal, sinking fund, emergency fund) and Yes or No for Done - rename them to match how you work
- START HERE tab - plain instructions, so you are set up within minutes
- Two copies in one download: a clean BLANK file and a filled EXAMPLE file with eleven sample funds to explore first

WHY IT HELPS

- Needed per month counts this month but not the month of the target date, so the money is there before the bill is
- Put in this month's share and the number stays the same until next month - it does not shrink while you are still saving
- A fund turns red when its target date has passed and it is not full, or when more was taken out than saved
- A fund turns amber when its target date is 60 days away or closer and it is not full, or when what you plan to put in each month is below what it needs. You can change the 60 days on SETUP
- A fund you mark Done never turns red or amber, and a full fund or a fund with no deadline never turns amber
- A transaction with no date, no fund, no amount or a fund that is not on FUNDS turns red, and the dashboard counts how many are waiting to be fixed
- A transaction dated after today turns amber and counts from that day on, so a scheduled transfer does not inflate what you have saved
- Moving money between funds is two rows: out of one, into the other
- No macros, no add-ons, no account - just a spreadsheet you own

HOW IT WORKS

1. Open in Excel or upload to Google Drive and open with Sheets
2. On FUNDS, add each fund: the target amount, the target date (or none), what is in it today and what you plan to put in each month
3. Log every deposit and withdrawal after that on TRANSACTIONS - pick the fund from the dropdown
4. Check FUNDS and DASHBOARD to see what each fund needs this month, and MONTHLY for the whole year

INSTANT DIGITAL DOWNLOAD

- One ZIP file, delivered by Etsy right after checkout: a BLANK working copy and a filled EXAMPLE copy (.xlsx)
- Works in Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets
- No physical item will be shipped
- For personal use - not for resale

This workbook is a savings planner, not financial advice. Your bank statements stay the official record.

results.description:
Keep every savings goal in one simple spreadsheet: a sinking funds tracker where each fund has its own goal, target date and monthly plan, a log for every deposit and withdrawal, and an overview that shows how much you have saved, how much is left and what each fund needs per month. Use it as a savings tracker, a savings goal tracker or a money goals planner for an emergency fund, a vacation fund, holiday gifts, car repairs or a yearly bill.
Opens in both Google Sheets and Microsoft Excel - every formula result was compared in Google Sheets and matched Excel (Excel's sheet protection does not carry over to Google Sheets). A worked example and a blank copy in the same download. No macros, no add-ins, any currency.
Made for anyone who sets money aside on purpose: register each fund once, then write one line for every deposit or withdrawal. The balances, the progress bars and the monthly totals update by themselves. Tables, colors and charts only - it does not connect to a bank.
This is an independent template made by Yamada Studio. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by any bank, credit union, payment app, budgeting app or brand. It is an organizational tool, not financial advice.

WHAT YOU RECEIVE

- 1 editable Excel workbook (.XLSX), filled in as a worked example for a fictional saver in October
- 1 blank workbook, ready to use
- 1 Quick Start Guide PDF
- License (TXT) and Read Me / disclaimer (TXT)
- One ZIP, six files, 115 KB. Instant digital download; no physical item will be shipped
- Google Sheets access PDF: two copy links (worked example and blank). Open a link, sign in to Google, press Make a copy, and the workbook is saved to your own Drive.

THE SEVEN SHEETS

1. Overview - four cards (total saved, left to save, overall progress, added this month), a progress bar for every fund, and the next target dates with what is left and needed per month.
2. Funds - up to 12 sinking funds: name, goal, target date, starting balance, your monthly plan and where it is kept (savings account, cash envelope and so on - rename the list). Deposits, withdrawals, balance, left to save, progress, months left, needed per month and a status are worked out.
3. Log - 300 lines: date, fund, deposit or withdrawal, amount and notes. Each line is checked, and a line with a problem says what to fix.
4. Monthly - deposits by month for each fund, the withdrawals and what was saved overall, with a chart.
5. Progress - one printable page: twenty boxes per fund, each 5% of the goal, that fill in by themselves as the balance grows.
6. Setup - your name, the year, the currency symbol and your own list of places you keep your savings.
7. Read Me - how it works, inside the workbook.

HOW IT WORKS

- Balance = starting balance + deposits - withdrawals.
- Needed per month = left to save divided by the months left to the target date. Simple division: no interest is added anywhere.
- Status: Reached, On track (your monthly plan covers what is needed), Behind (it does not), Saving (no target date or plan yet) or Date passed.
- A figure that cannot be worked out is left blank, not shown as nought.

IT DOES NOT

- Connect to a bank or any account, download transactions or move money - you type what you did.
- Work out interest or returns, or tell you how much to save or where to keep it.
- Send reminders.

results.title: Savings Tracker Spreadsheet, Goals with Target Dates and Monthly Amounts (Google Sheets & Excel)
results.description:
A savings tracker for Google Sheets and Excel. Name each goal, its date and what's put aside, and see how close each one is and what it takes per month.

One tab is the whole product. Each thing you're saving for gets a row: what it is, what it will cost, the date you need it by, and how much you've put aside so far. From those four the tab works out the rest: what's still to go, how many months are left, what that is per month, how complete the goal is, and a bar so you can see it at a glance. Across the top, the same for all your goals together: saved so far, the total you're aiming at, what's still to go, what it takes per month to stay on track, and how many goals are fully funded.

What it does for you

- Every goal on one page. Up to twelve at once: holiday gifts, new tires, the emergency fund, a vacation, the deductible. Each with its own target, date and progress, so you can see which one is nearly there.
- How much per month. Give a goal a date and the tab divides what's left by the months until then. Move the date, or put more aside, and the figure follows.
- How close each one is. A percentage and a bar for every goal, and a count of how many are fully funded. When a goal gets there, it reads 100%, the bar is full, and its per-month figure drops to zero.
- Where you stand, in five numbers. Saved so far, target total, still to go, per month to stay on track, and goals fully funded, across the top of the tab with a bar of the whole.
- One figure to keep up to date. "Saved so far" is a single amount for each goal. When you move money, type the new total over the old one. That's the whole routine.
- Hard to break by accident. Colored cells are yours to type in. Everything else is locked so the numbers keep working.
- Four color themes in one file. Shore, Meadow, Slate and Midnight, switched from a dropdown on the tab. There is nothing to choose at checkout.
- One tab, on its own. Copy it for more goals, or one for each person, and every copy works by itself.

What's in the download

- Sortment Savings Tracker.xlsx, filled with example goals so you can see it working
- Sortment Savings Tracker - blank.xlsx, the same tab, empty, for your own goals
- A quick-start PDF with the two Google Sheets links (example and blank). Open one, choose File > Make a copy, and it's yours.

How it works

1. Name each goal. What it's for and what it will cost. Add the date you need it by, if there is one.
2. Type what you've put aside so far. One figure per goal.
3. Read the row. Still to go, months left, per month, and how complete it is.
4. When you move money, update "Saved so far". Type the new total over the old one, and everything else catches up.

Compatibility

- Google Sheets and Excel. Use whichever you prefer, or both.
- Nothing to install, no add-ons, no subscription, no bank connection. You type what you've put aside, and the tab does the rest.
- It opens in the Google Sheets or Excel app on your phone, so a goal can be updated wherever you are.
- The font is Montserrat, which is free. Install it for the exact look in Excel, or skip it. Everything works without it.
- It comes in dollars. Changing the currency is ordinary cell formatting, and the quick-start shows where.

Questions

Is this a physical item?
No. It's a digital download: two Excel files, a PDF quick-start, and links to copy the Google Sheets versions. Nothing is mailed.

Does it keep a list of every deposit?
No. Each goal has one "Saved so far" figure, and you type the new total over it when you move money. There is no list of deposits and no month-by-month history. That is what keeps the whole thing to one page.

Is this a savings challenge?
No. There are no squares to color in and no set amounts to follow. You choose the goals, the amounts and the dates, and the tab does the arithmetic.

Does it work out interest?
No. It divides what's left by the months left, and that's all. There's no interest rate, no growth and no forecast. It's for money you're putting aside, not money you're investing.

What if a goal has no date?
It still counts in saved so far, target total and still to go. It just has no months left and no per-month figure, and a note under the table says so. Add a date whenever you want one.

What if the date has already passed?
The tab treats it as one month left, so the per-month figure is everything that's still to go. Move the date and it recalculates.

What if I've put aside more than the target?
Still to go shows zero, the goal reads 100% and the bar is full. Nothing goes negative.

Does it connect to my bank?
No. A spreadsheet can't read your bank, and this one doesn't try. You type the figure, and the rest is done the moment you do.

I have more than twelve goals.
Copy the tab and carry on in the copy. Each copy works on its own, with its own totals.

Is this a budget?
No. There's no income here, no categories and no spending. It's the savings goals on their own. If you want them inside a full budget, the shop's full budget workbook has this same table as one of its tabs.

Is it one tab, really?
Yes. The goals, the totals and the readouts across the top are all on the one tab.

Do I get Google Sheets or Excel?
Both. Same tab, same four themes. For Google Sheets, use the Make a copy link in your quick-start guide. An Excel file you upload to Google Drive yourself works, but loses the protection that warns you before you type over a formula.

Do I pick a theme when I order?
No. All four themes are in the one file. Pick one from the dropdown on the tab and change it any time.

What if I type over something I shouldn't?
Undo puts it back. The cells that do the work are locked, so it's hard to do by accident. For a clean start, open the blank file or make a fresh copy from the Google Sheets link.

License and support

Sortment Savings Tracker is licensed for your own personal use. Please don't share, resell, or repost the files. If a friend wants one, point them to the shop.

Because this is a digital file, Etsy doesn't allow returns once it's downloaded. If something isn't working the way you expect, message me on Etsy with what's happening (a screenshot helps) and I'll help you get it sorted. I usually reply within one business day.

Debt Reconciliation — Net balances for every person in the group. A zero-sum check at the bottom confirms the math nets to zero — so you know the numbers are right before anyone sends anything.

My Expenses — Select a name from the dropdown, see only that person's charges and who they need to pay. Useful when someone asks "wait, what do I actually owe?" and you don't want to walk them through the whole ledger.

Weekend Itinerary — Day-by-day schedule for the bachelorette weekend with times, activities, and who fronted each event.

Task Tracker — Planning to-do list with deadlines, owner, and status. Overdue rows turn red automatically.

Roster — One place for contact info, dress size, dietary needs, budget cap, and all three payment handles. Also includes an income-proportional split model for fixed shared costs — useful when the group's incomes vary significantly and equal splitting isn't realistic.

results.title: Rental Income and Expense Tracker Spreadsheet for Landlords | Excel & Google Sheets Rental Property Bookkeeping | Rent Roll Template
results.description:
Rental income and expense tracker for landlords with 1 to 10 rentals. Log rent and bills, see who paid on the rent roll, and get Schedule E-style totals. Excel.

Know who paid, where the money went, and what to hand your tax preparer, all in one spreadsheet.

This is a simple bookkeeping workbook for small landlords with 1 to 10 rental properties. Log rent and expenses as they happen. The 12-month rent roll marks every unit Paid, Late, Partial or Unpaid automatically. The dashboard shows monthly and year-to-date income, expenses and net cash flow for each property and in total. At year end, the Schedule E-style summary lists your totals by property in the same line order as IRS Schedule E, so you or your preparer can transfer them.

It's built for buy-and-hold landlords with single-family homes, duplexes and small multifamily. The example data has a St. Louis-area flavor (St. Louis City and Jefferson County, MO), and it works for rentals anywhere in the US.

What's inside (8 tabs, 1 .xlsx file):
- Instructions: plain-English setup, a 2-minute "clear the example" guide, how every number is calculated, tips and the disclaimer.
- Dashboard: choose any property (or All) and a month. You get KPIs (income, operating expenses, principal + improvements, net cash flow, rent collection rate, deposits held), a 12-month cash-flow table, expenses by category, a per-property table and 2 charts.
- Properties: up to 10 properties with nickname, address, units, property type, purchase date and price, and rental days. Every property drop-down reads from this list.
- Income Log: 600 rows for date, property, unit/tenant, type (Rent, Late fee, Other income, Security deposit held), amount and notes. An optional "For month" column handles rent paid early or late.
- Expense Log: 800 rows for date, property, vendor, category, amount, receipt saved? and notes. The categories follow Schedule E: advertising, auto & travel, cleaning & maintenance, commissions, insurance, legal & professional, management fees, mortgage interest, other interest, repairs, supplies, taxes, utilities, depreciation (placeholder) and other. Mortgage principal and capital improvements are tracked separately so they don't inflate your deductions.
- Rent Roll: 25 unit/tenant rows. A 12-month color-coded grid (Paid / Late / Partial / Unpaid / Due / Vacant) fills itself from the Income Log, with rent collected, rent due, balance owed and collection rate.
- Schedule E Summary: lines 3 to 21 for each of up to 10 properties plus a total column. A separate "for your records" block shows principal, improvements, deposits, late fees and net cash flow. It's an organizer, not a tax form.
- Lists: the category-to-Schedule E line map.

Why landlords like this format:
- Type only in the yellow cells. Formulas are locked so they can't be broken by accident, and protection has no password, so you can customize.
- Missing a property or category? The cell turns red. Is a date outside your tax year? It turns amber.
- No macros, no add-ons, no subscription. It uses standard functions only.
- It comes pre-filled with a clearly labeled EXAMPLE portfolio (hypothetical properties, tenants and vendors) so you can see every tab working before you add your own data.

Works with: Microsoft Excel (desktop, web and Mac) and Google Sheets (upload the .xlsx to Google Drive and open it). It also opens in LibreOffice.

You'll receive: Landlord_Rental_Tracker.xlsx and Buyer_Quick_Start.pdf (1 page).

Important: This is a record-keeping and organizing tool. It is not tax, legal, accounting or financial advice, and the Schedule E Summary is not a tax form or tax return. Category names and line numbers are a convenience based on IRS Schedule E (Form 1040). Tax treatment (depreciation, repairs vs. improvements, security deposits, passive loss limits, personal use) depends on your situation, so please review with a qualified tax professional. Results are only as accurate as the numbers you enter. The example data is hypothetical and doesn't represent typical results.

Digital download: no physical item will be shipped. Personal-use license. Please don't resell or redistribute.

FAQ

What do I get?
One Excel file (.xlsx) with 8 tabs (Instructions, Dashboard, Properties, Income Log, Expense Log, Rent Roll, Schedule E Summary, Lists) and a 1-page quick start PDF. It's an instant digital download.

Does it work in Google Sheets?
Yes. Upload the .xlsx to Google Drive, then open it with Google Sheets (or use File > Import). It uses only standard functions such as SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, IF and DATE, and has no macros. One note: Google Sheets doesn't keep Excel's locked-cell protection. The formulas still work, so just type only in the yellow cells.

Does it work on Mac?
Yes, in Excel for Mac or in Google Sheets. Apple Numbers may open it, but it isn't officially supported.

How many properties and units?
Up to 10 properties, 25 unit/tenant rows on the rent roll, 600 income rows and 800 expense rows per year. That's plenty for a small landlord's year.

Is this a tax form? Will it do my taxes?
No. The Schedule E Summary is an organizer that totals what you logged in the same order as Schedule E. It doesn't file anything, calculate depreciation or apply loss limits. The depreciation line is a placeholder for the figure from your tax preparer. Please review everything with a qualified tax professional.

How does the rent roll know who paid?
It reads Rent entries in the Income Log that match the property and unit/tenant label. Full rent by your "late after" day shows Paid, full rent after that shows Late, some rent shows Partial, and nothing past the late day shows Unpaid. Months outside the lease dates show Vacant.

What about security deposits?
Log them as "Security deposit (held)". They're shown separately and aren't counted as income. If you keep part of a deposit (for damages, for example), log that part as "Other income".

How do I clear the example data?
The Instructions tab lists 4 ranges. Select each one and press Delete (about 2 minutes). Only the yellow cells clear, and the formulas stay.

Can I use it next year?
Yes. Keep a blank copy, or change the tax year on the Properties tab and start new logs.

Can I change the formulas?
Yes. Sheets are protected without a password. In Excel, go to Review > Unprotect Sheet.

Is the example real?
No. The pre-filled properties, addresses, tenants, vendors and amounts are a labeled hypothetical EXAMPLE for illustration only. They aren't typical or expected results.
