results.title: Etsy Seller Bookkeeping Spreadsheet | Google Sheets and Excel Tracker for Etsy Fees, Profit and Loss, Expenses, Mileage, Sales Tax
results.description:
Etsy deposits are not your profit. Between transaction fees, processing fees, listing renewals, Offsite Ads, postage and materials, it's hard to know what you actually earned until tax time, when it's too late to fix. Etsy Seller Bookkeeping keeps a running answer, month by month, in one spreadsheet that works in Google Sheets (free) and Excel.

What's inside (15 tabs)
- Dashboard: net revenue, Etsy fees (and fees as % of sales), net profit and margin, tax to set aside, average order value, a month-by-month profit trend, top 5 products, where the money went, sales by channel, and a to-do list (uncategorised expenses, missing receipts, duplicate orders, months missing a statement total, sales tax owed).
- Sales: one row per order, with channel, item, qty, item sales, discount, shipping, sales tax and refunds. For Etsy orders it estimates the 6.5% transaction fee, the 3% + $0.25 processing fee, the $0.20 renewal and the Offsite Ads fee (capped at $100). Duplicate order numbers turn red.
- CSV Import: paste Etsy's Orders CSV (and, optionally, the Order Items CSV) and the orders come out lined up in Sales column order, with a ✓ check that each total matches. Product names come from your SKUs or listing titles, and orders you've already entered are highlighted. Every column is found by its header name, so column order doesn't matter, and a missing column is left blank instead of breaking the sheet.
- Fee Check: estimated fees next to the fee total on your Etsy monthly statement. Once you enter the real figure, the P&L uses it.
- Expenses: 17 categories (materials, packaging, postage, Etsy Ads, subscriptions, booth fees and more), each with a suggested Schedule C line. Receipt tracking included.
- Mileage: business trips at the IRS standard rate. Both 2026 rates (72.5¢ to June 30, 76¢ from July 1) are built in, and the right one applies to each trip date.
- Products & Pricing: profit per item after materials, packaging, postage and Etsy fees, the lowest price that keeps a 50% margin, and units and revenue sold.
- Monthly P&L: revenue, cost of goods sold, gross profit, selling costs, operating expenses, net profit and margin for each month and the whole year.
- Sales Tax: separates the tax Etsy collects and pays for you from tax you collected at craft fairs or on your own site, with paid/owed tracking.
- Tax Summary: year totals laid out like Schedule C (lines 1-31), checked against the P&L, plus estimated self-employment and income tax, quarterly estimated payment amounts and a payment log.
- Settings and Lists: fee rates, tax rates, mileage rates and every dropdown, all editable for non-US shops or future fee changes.

You get
- Etsy-Seller-Bookkeeping-Example.xlsx, a year of made-up data for an imaginary paper-goods shop so you can see the numbers flow through, and Etsy-Seller-Bookkeeping-Blank.xlsx, ready for your shop.
- A 2-page PDF guide covering opening the workbook in Google Sheets (File > Import, or upload to Drive and open with Sheets) or Excel, plus the 15-minute monthly routine and troubleshooting.
- A Start Here tab with instructions inside the workbook.
- Works in Google Sheets (free), Excel 2010 or later on Windows, Excel 2011 or later on Mac, and Microsoft 365. No add-ons, macros or scripts.

Honest notes
- Not tax, legal or accounting advice, and not affiliated with or endorsed by Etsy, Inc. Check your figures and categories with a tax professional.
- Per-order fees are estimates based on Etsy's published US rates as of October 2026. Real statements can differ (refund credits, currency conversion, regulatory fees), which is why Fee Check lets you enter the real total. If Etsy changes its fees, update the rates on Settings.
- The tax set-aside is a simple US sole-proprietor estimate (SE tax + your chosen income tax rate). It ignores the QBI deduction, credits, other income and state rules.
- CSV column names couldn't be confirmed with Etsy. Etsy's help pages explain how to download the Orders and Order Items CSVs (Shop Manager > Settings > Options > Download Data) but don't publish their column names. The names built in come from public sample exports and from third-party tools that read these files. To make that safe, the import looks every column up by name, shows which ones it found, leaves missing ones blank, and lets you retype a name if Etsy changes it. Check the ✓ column before copying rows into Sales. Mark Offsite Ads orders yourself (the CSV doesn't say which orders they are).
- Outside the US, change the fee rates, treat the Sales Tax tab as a VAT/GST tracker and ignore the Schedule C labels.
- Built by an AI agent, with every formula checked against an independent calculation (760+ checks), and the import tested with shuffled and missing CSV columns. All example data is made up.
- In Excel, click "Enable Editing" when the file first opens. Until you do, totals can look blank. The fonts (Poppins, Roboto) are built into Google Sheets; Excel substitutes a similar font if they aren't installed.

License: Use it for your own business, with a new copy each year. Please don't resell or share the files.

Requirements: A free Google account (Google Sheets) or Microsoft Excel 2010 or later / Microsoft 365.

Format: Instant digital download: 2 .xlsx workbooks (example and blank) + a 2-page PDF guide.

results.title: Bookkeeping Spreadsheet for Etsy Sellers, Profit and Loss Dashboard, Fee Calculator, Income Expense Tracker, Excel, Google Sheets
results.description:
See every fee. Know your real profit.
Paste in your Etsy CSVs and the sheet does the rest. Your deposit isn't your profit. The Seller Bookkeeping & Profit Dashboard is an instant-download spreadsheet that breaks out the Etsy fees on every order and shows your Gross profit (what's left after Etsy fees, product cost and Etsy postage labels), order by order and month by month. Made for US and Australian sellers, it works with any Etsy shop currency, in Excel for Microsoft 365, Excel for the web and Google Sheets. No macros.

Digital download only. No physical item is shipped. You need Excel for Microsoft 365 on a laptop or desktop computer, Excel for the web, or Google Sheets.

Launch price until 30 Nov 2026. The regular price applies from 1 Dec. Etsy shows the price in your own currency at checkout.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Pick your preset. In Settings, choose your currency and the US or AU Etsy fee preset (or enter your own rates), then answer the GST and Offsite Ads questions.
2. Paste your Etsy CSVs. Paste the Orders CSV you download from your shop into the Orders Import tab (the Order Items CSV and your monthly statement CSV are optional). The Fee Breakout fills in.
3. Add costs and other sales. List your products and unit costs, log your expenses and any sales from markets, wholesale or your website, and your monthly P&L and dashboard fill in.

No subscription, no macros, no add-ons. It does not connect to your shop: you paste in files you download yourself, so your data stays with you.

EVERY FEE ON EVERY ORDER

Fees come out in lots of small lines that are easy to miss. The Fee Breakout tab lists every imported order with its fees worked out line by line:

- Listing fee
- Transaction fee
- Payment processing fee (domestic and international rates)
- Offsite Ads fee (only on orders that came from an Etsy ad, with Etsy's US$100 per-order cap)
- Currency conversion fee (only when an order's currency differs from your bank currency)
- GST on fees (Australian shops only: switch it on if you have no ABN on file)

Then it shows total Etsy fees, your net payout, product cost, Etsy postage labels, and your Gross profit (net sales minus Etsy fees, product cost and postage labels) and margin for that order.

Offsite Ads orders are flagged in one of two ways: paste in your monthly statement on the Statement Import tab, or type their order IDs into Settings. Otherwise no Offsite Ads fee is added.

Fees are estimates worked out from the preset rates in Settings, not the exact amounts Etsy charged. If you paste in your monthly statement too, the Statement Import tab shows Etsy's own fee totals next to the estimates so you can compare.

MADE FOR US AND AUSTRALIAN SELLERS

- US sellers: pick the Etsy US preset and your US Etsy fees are built in.
- Australian sellers: pick the Etsy AU preset for Australian Etsy fees, plus a GST-on-fees switch.
- Anywhere else: works with any Etsy shop currency (for example US$, A$, £ or €). Choose yours in Settings and type in your own rates.

For example, on a $20 domestic sale both presets work out a 6.5% transaction fee ($1.30) and 3% + $0.25 payment processing ($0.85), in your shop currency.

- Etsy US preset: 6.5% transaction, US$0.20 listing, 3% + US$0.25 payment processing, based on Etsy's published US rates as of Oct 2026. Please check Etsy for changes.
- Etsy AU preset: 6.5% transaction, 3% + A$0.25 payment processing on domestic orders or 4% + A$0.25 on international orders, US$0.20 listing, Offsite Ads at 15% (or 12% once your shop has made US$10K in a year) when it applies, 2.5% currency conversion when it applies, and 10% GST on fees if you have no ABN on file. These are Etsy's current AU fees as of Oct 2026. Please check Etsy for changes.

Every rate is an editable cell, with a Custom column for your own rates. If Etsy changes a fee or your statement shows something different, update one number and the whole workbook follows. Selling from another country? Type in your own rates.

WHAT'S INSIDE (12 TABS)

1. Start Here: 3-step setup, links to every tab, a key showing which cells you edit, and how to clear the sample data when you are ready.
2. Settings: business name, currency, estimated tax rate and the month your fiscal year starts (so a July to June year works). The US/AU Etsy fee preset, GST and Offsite Ads switches, other sales channels you can rename, and your expense categories.
3. Orders Import: paste your Etsy Orders CSV here. Columns are found by name, and Etsy's month/day/year dates are converted for you. Any date it can't read, or can't tell day from month, is flagged in red so you can check it and set the date order in Settings.
4. Items Import (optional): paste the Order Items CSV to add product costs and per-product stats.
5. Statement Import (optional): paste your monthly statements to find Offsite Ads orders and Etsy postage labels, and compare Etsy's fee totals with the estimates.
6. Fee Breakout: every imported order with its fees broken out line by line, net payout and Gross profit. Nothing to type on this tab.
7. Sales Log: for sales outside the import (markets, wholesale, your website). Fees, product cost and Gross profit calculate on each row.
8. Expenses Log: every business cost with date, category, vendor, amount, a tax-deductible Yes/No flag and a receipt note.
9. Products: your SKU list with unit cost and sale price, plus units sold, revenue, fees, product cost and Gross profit for each product.
10. Monthly P&L: a 12-month profit and loss that follows your fiscal year. Revenue, selling fees, product cost, gross profit, expenses by category, net profit after expenses, margins and a year-to-date total.
11. Dashboard: 8 KPI tiles (revenue, net profit after expenses, net margin, orders, average order value, fees paid, operating expenses, top product by Gross profit), 4 charts, a "Where your Etsy fees went" table and a period selector for the full year or any single month.
12. Tax Summary: deductible vs non-deductible spending by category, estimated taxable profit, an estimated tax set-aside at a rate you choose, and a quarterly breakdown. Handy to have ready for your accountant. It is an estimate, not tax advice.

Room for 1,500 imported orders, 5,000 Sales Log rows, 5,000 expenses and 500 products. It arrives with sample data from a fictional shop so you can see it working before you add your own.

WHICH APP YOU NEED

- Works in Excel for Microsoft 365, Excel for the web and Google Sheets. An .xlsx workbook with standard formulas and no macros.
- Other Excel versions and Apple Numbers are not supported yet.
- Best on a laptop or desktop computer.

WHAT YOU GET

This is an instant digital download:

- The Seller Bookkeeping & Profit Dashboard workbook (.xlsx), filled with sample data you can clear
- A step-by-step How To Use guide (PDF) and a one-page Quick Start (PDF)
- A README with the setup steps

Etsy does not accept spreadsheet files directly, so the download comes as one ZIP file. After checkout, download it from your Etsy Purchases page (or the link in your receipt email), unzip it, and open the workbook. Download from a web browser on etsy.com (Purchases page), because the Etsy app can't download digital files. On a phone, save the file and open it later on a computer.

WHO IT'S FOR

- Small Etsy sellers who want to know what each order really made after fees, not just total sales

FAQ

1. Which spreadsheet apps is it for?
It works in Excel for Microsoft 365 on a laptop or desktop computer, in Excel for the web and in Google Sheets. It is an .xlsx workbook with standard formulas and no macros. Other Excel versions and Apple Numbers are not supported yet.

2. Can I use it in Google Sheets?
Yes. It works in Google Sheets as well as in Excel for Microsoft 365 and Excel for the web. If anything looks wrong in Sheets, send me a message and I'll help.

3. Will it work for my country?
Yes. It works with any Etsy shop currency. US and Australian sellers can use the built-in Etsy US or Etsy AU fee presets, and every fee rate, the currency symbol and the fiscal year start month can be changed. If you sell from another country, enter your own Etsy rates from your payment account statement.

4. Does it connect to my Etsy shop?
No. You download CSV files from your shop and paste them in. Nothing is linked to your account.

5. Does it do my taxes or file anything for me?
No. It is a bookkeeping and tracking spreadsheet. The Tax Summary tab gives you an estimated set-aside, using a tax rate you enter. It is not tax, accounting or financial advice. Please check with your accountant or your local tax authority.

6. How do I import my Etsy CSV?
Download your Orders CSV from your Etsy shop, open it, copy everything including the header row, and paste it into cell B8 of the Orders Import tab. Do the same for the Order Items and statement CSVs if you want them. To update later, first select cell B9 down to the last row of each Import tab and press Delete, then paste the new CSV at B8. Pasting over the old data can leave old orders behind. The Start Here tab walks you through it.

7. What about refunds?
Refunds on imported Etsy orders are not taken off automatically. Enter them by hand as a discount line in the Sales Log. For sales you type in, enter the refunded amount in the Discount column.

8. What about different currencies?
The workbook keeps your books in one currency, which you choose in Settings (for example US$, A$, £ or €). If an order is in a different currency from your bank, the currency conversion fee shows as its own line, using a rate you can edit.

9. Can I get a refund?

If I improve or fix the workbook, the listing file is updated. Message me through Etsy any time and I will help you get the latest version.

11. Do I need to be good at spreadsheets?
No. You paste your CSVs and type into the navy-header columns and the amber settings cells. Everything else calculates. Formula columns have slate headers, so just avoid typing over them. Expense categories and channel names are editable in Settings.

results.title: Canadian Bookkeeping Spreadsheet Excel, Google Sheets CRA T2125 GST
results.description:
Come tax time, your T2125 totals and the GST/HST to remit are already added up, and all year it shows how much to put aside for tax. This Canadian bookkeeping spreadsheet is for self-employed people: you record income, expenses, mileage and home office costs as you go, in Excel or Google Sheets.

“So easy to use and for what I need for my consulting business, this is perfect!” (R., review of this listing, August 2026)

QUICK FACTS
• For sole proprietors, freelancers and contractors who file a T2125. If you're incorporated, it's probably not the right fit
• An Excel workbook and a Google Sheets copy, for one price with no subscription
• 2026 rates for all 13 provinces and territories, with the source beside each one
• GST/HST worked out on every sale by place of supply, plus input tax credits and a tax estimate with CPP or QPP
• 16 tabs and 8 charts, with no macros, so neither Google nor Excel shows a warning
• It comes filled in with a sample year, so you can see a finished year before you clear it
• Setup is six answers on START HERE and takes about five minutes

The video in the photos shows the real workbook. Questions before or after you buy? Message me through Etsy. I usually reply within a few hours.

Most bookkeeping templates are American. They're built around Schedule C and US sales tax, which leaves you translating everything for the CRA at tax time. This one is set up for the T2125 and Canadian sales tax.

It's for sole proprietors, freelancers, contractors, consultants, side hustlers and online sellers without inventory who keep their own books. It isn't full accounting software. It doesn't do payroll, inventory, bill tracking, T2 corporate returns, multiple users or bank feeds.

WHAT IT HANDLES FOR YOU
• Place of supply on every sale. Each income row has its own province, so an Ontario designer billing a client in Alberta charges 5% GST instead of 13% HST.
• Input tax credits. If you're registered and claim back the GST/HST on a purchase, the deduction is the cost before tax. If you can't claim it, you deduct the full amount you paid.
• PST stays in the cost of what you bought, because you can't get it back. The workbook treats QST the same way (see the Quebec question below).
• Meals at 50%. Half the cost is deductible and only half the tax on it can be claimed back.
• Business use of home is capped at your business income before the claim, as the rule requires. Anything over the cap shows as a carry-forward instead of disappearing.
• A tax estimate worked out band by band: federal brackets, your provincial or territorial brackets, the federal and provincial basic personal amounts, CPP with the second tier (or QPP in Quebec) and the Quebec abatement.
• The 2026 vehicle limits: leases up to $1,100 a month before tax and car loan interest up to $350 a month. It tells you if your lease payment is over the limit.

THE 16 TABS

START HERE: a five-minute walkthrough of the six setup answers
SETUP: province, tax year, GST/HST registration and reporting period
TAX TABLES: every rate the workbook uses, with its source beside it
CATEGORIES: 26 expense categories and 8 income categories, each mapped to its T2125 line
INCOME: 600 rows. Type what you received, tax included, and it splits the tax out
EXPENSES: 900 rows. Pick a category and a business-use percentage and it works out the credit and the deduction
MILEAGE: 300 trips, plus what the vehicle cost, with the lease and interest limits applied
HOME OFFICE: work area, home area and running costs, capped so the claim can't create a loss
DASHBOARD: the year on one screen, including the GST/HST to remit and the tax to set aside
YEAR AT A GLANCE: every month, category and quarter, with in-cell bars
MONTH: pick a month and see it against the rest of the year
T2125 SUMMARY: your totals in the order the form asks for them, with line numbers
GST-HST: tax collected against credits, by month and by quarter, with your filing position
TAX ESTIMATE: federal tax, provincial tax and CPP or QPP, band by band, with a monthly set-aside
DEADLINES: every date that matters for the tax year you entered
FAQ: common questions, answered inside the file

The sample year is a made-up Toronto design studio. Clear its entries from the pale cream cells and every total goes back to zero.

THE RATES
Every rate was checked against canada.ca, the Department of Finance or Revenu Québec on 17 September 2026, and the file lists the source next to each one. That includes Nova Scotia's 14% HST, the $74,600 CPP ceiling with the second tier up to $85,000, the $16,452 federal basic personal amount, and the per-kilometre rates of 73 and 67 cents (77 and 71 in the territories).

You can set it to any tax year. When rates change, type the new ones into TAX TABLES and every calculation follows them, or message me and I'll send you the updated file. Updates are free for the life of the product.

QUESTIONS

Do I need to be good with spreadsheets?
No. You type in the pale cream cells and leave everything else alone. The categories are drop-downs, and START HERE walks you through the six setup answers.

Will it tell me exactly what I owe the CRA?
No, and I'd be wary of anything that claims it can. It gives you planning figures from what you enter. Your actual bill depends on your other income, credits, deductions, RRSP contributions, instalments you've already paid and more. Use the estimate to put money aside. For the final number, go by your return or ask your accountant.

Can I give it to my accountant?
Yes. T2125 SUMMARY lists your year in the order the form asks for it, with the line number beside each figure. That's a lot easier for them to work from than twelve months of bank statements.

Do I need both Excel and Google Sheets?
No. You get both and use whichever you have. The Excel file doesn't need a Google account, and the Google Sheets copy only needs a free one and a browser.

I'm not registered for GST/HST. Is it still useful?
Yes. Set registration to No on SETUP and it won't charge tax or claim credits, and it deducts expenses at the full amount you paid. You have to register once your worldwide taxable revenue passes $30,000 in one calendar quarter or over four quarters in a row. The DASHBOARD warns you as you get close.

I'm in Quebec. Will it work for me?
Mostly. Choose Quebec and it uses the QPP rates and the Quebec abatement on federal tax. It keeps QST in the cost of your purchases and doesn't track QST input tax refunds. If you're registered for QST, check your QST refunds and any other Quebec rules with Revenu Québec or an accountant.

Can I ask you a question after I buy?
Yes. Message me through Etsy. I usually reply within a few hours, and I'm happy to help with anything in the workbook.

Choosing a province doesn't change the place-of-supply rules. You're still responsible for which taxes you're registered for, which rate applies, whether a sale is taxable, zero-rated or exempt, and whether a purchase qualifies for a credit.

Rates and rules change, so confirm the current requirements with canada.ca, Revenu Québec where it applies, your provincial authority or a qualified accountant before you file or remit.

Bookkeeping and GST spreadsheet made for New Zealand sole traders and small businesses. Paste in your bank CSV, let your own rules suggest the coding, reconcile to the cent, and get your GST return figures box by box. NZD, 15% GST, a 1 April – 31 March year, and NZ bank CSV formats.

Made by Devery Foster in Wellington (EY audit experience, Xero Associate, BCom).

INSTANT DIGITAL DOWNLOAD – nothing is posted.

WHAT YOU GET
• BLANK workbook (.xlsx), ready for your own data
• EXAMPLE workbook (.xlsx), filled in for a fictional Wellington painter so you can see how it all works
• Google Sheets "Make a copy" links (in the guide) for both versions
• Quick-start guide (PDF, 4 pages)
• Licence and terms (PDF)

WHAT IT DOES
• Bank Import: paste your CSV columns, pick the account, and your rules suggest the business, category and job. It flags lines that are already in your ledger. Includes a column guide for ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac and Kiwibank exports.
• Rules: "payee contains…" rules, checked top to bottom. First match wins.
• Ledger: one list for up to 5 businesses plus Personal. Category and job dropdowns follow the business you pick. GST, net amount and checks fill in automatically. Room for 1,000 lines.
• Reconciliation: each bank account must tie to your statement to the cent (PASS/CHECK). Also checks for uncategorised lines, possible duplicates, personal/business mix-ups and unknown categories.
• P&L: by business and month, plus year to date and a detailed P&L for each business. GST-exclusive when you're registered.
• Job Profit: income, costs and margin for every job.
• GST worksheet: Boxes 5 to 15 for each monthly, 2-monthly or 6-monthly period, including zero-rated sales, adjustment boxes and usual due dates.

• Dashboard: income, expenses, profit, GST, bank and lowest-cash figures, with charts.

PLEASE READ BEFORE YOU BUY – WHAT IT DOESN'T DO
• No live bank feeds. You download CSV files from your internet banking and paste them in.
• GST on the payments basis only. If you use the invoice or hybrid basis, you'll need to make adjustments yourself.
• It doesn't file anything. Copy the figures into myIR yourself, or give them to your accountant.
• No invoicing, payroll/PAYE, stock or depreciation, and no balance sheet. It's a cash-basis bookkeeping workbook, not full accounting software.

WHAT YOU NEED

FAQ
Q: Is this suitable for me if I'm not GST registered?
A: Yes. Set "GST registered?" to No on the Cover. GST amounts become zero, and the P&L and reports use your full amounts. The GST sheet is then for reference only.

Q: Does it connect to my bank?
A: No. There are no live bank feeds. You export a CSV from internet banking (ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac, Kiwibank and others) and paste the columns into the Bank Import sheet. The guide shows which column goes where for each bank.

Q: Which GST basis does it use?
A: The payments basis only. It works from bank lines. If you use the invoice or hybrid basis, add unpaid invoices and bills yourself or use the adjustment boxes (9 and 13).

Q: Will it file my GST return?

Q: Can I change the categories?

Q: Is it tax advice?
A: No. It's a bookkeeping tool. It isn't tax or accounting advice. Check your GST and income tax with Inland Revenue or an accountant.

WHAT'S INSIDE (11 tabs)

• Deposits: your payouts to your bank

• Monthly Dashboard: year-to-date and chosen-month totals (sales, refunds, fees, expenses, net profit (bookkeeping total), margin, fees as a percentage of sales, orders), a 12-month table, expenses by category and three charts

results.title: Bookkeeping Spreadsheet Canada, T2125 Self Employed Tracker, Small Business GST HST, Dashboard, Excel, Google Sheets
results.description:
Self employed spreadsheet for Canada. Log your invoices and expenses, and each expense goes to its line on CRA Form T2125, with GST/HST worked out by quarter.
Made for freelancers, contractors and sole proprietors. The file opens on a Dashboard with your totals for the year, four charts and the lines for your tax return. It works in Excel, Google Sheets and Apple Numbers.

The Dashboard
You type nothing on this sheet. It fills in from your other sheets.
• A menu down the left side links to every sheet. It also shows your tax year, how many entries each log holds, how many clients you billed and whether a check needs a look.
• Two buttons at the top, Add an expense and Add a sale, take you to those logs.
• Six number cards across the top: sales, costs, GST/HST owing, invoices not paid yet, how much to set aside and net profit. The set aside card covers income tax, CPP and GST/HST, using a share of profit you choose on Setup.
• Four charts: sales and costs by month, where the money went (your five biggest T2125 lines and the rest), profit as a running total and sales by client (your five biggest clients and the rest).
• The amounts for your tax return with their line numbers: gross business income (8299), cost of goods sold (8518), total expenses (9368), net income before adjustments (9369), business use of home (9945) and your net income (9946). Under them is GST/HST for the year: what you charged, your input tax credits and what you owe, or the quick method amounts if that is your method.
• Six tables under the charts: month by month, GST/HST by quarter with the date to pay each one, what to set aside, costs by T2125 line, your top 10 clients and how many check messages each sheet has.
Sales by client goes by the name you type, so spell each client the same way every time.

The other sheets
• Start Here: how to use the file in short steps.
• Setup: your province, GST/HST details (with the date your registration took effect, if it was this year), fiscal year, home office areas and vehicle km.
• Rates: GST/HST rates for every province and territory, quick method rates, the meals share, vehicle limits (with a table for earlier years), the income tax instalment amounts and dates, and filing deadlines, each with its year and source.
• Income: 500 rows, one per invoice. GST/HST fills in from your province or your client's province. Pick Outside Canada for a client who is outside Canada and that sale gets 0%. Do not pick it for a client who is an individual in Canada while you work for them, or for a job on property in Canada: those sales carry GST/HST. A Date paid column shows which invoices are still unpaid.
• Expenses: 1,000 rows and 41 categories, each sent to its T2125 line, with a business use percent where it applies. Meals and entertainment count at 50%, and so do meals while you travel.
• Home Office: your business share from the work space area, with hours and days for a shared space. The claim cannot create a loss, and the rest carries forward.
• Vehicle: your business share from your km. Car loan interest and lease payments are held to the CRA limits for the days you had them, and a leased car gets both lease tests, list price included.
• T2125 Summary: Part 3 income (including quick method lines 3D to 3F and the 1% credit on line 8230), cost of goods sold, every Part 4 expense line and your net income.
• GST HST Summary: what you owe for each quarter and the year, with the regular method and input tax credits or the quick method, plus due dates. It tests the $30,000 small supplier limit by calendar quarter, the way the CRA does, and flags the $400,000 quick method limit and when a yearly filer may owe instalments.

Who it is for
Self employed Canadians who file Form T2125, from full time freelancers to side businesses, with or without a GST/HST number. Keep your totals ready for your return or for your accountant.

What you get
An instant download with 3 files:
• Canadian Self Employed Income Expense and HST Tracker T2125.xlsx: the blank file for your own records.
• Canadian Self Employed Income Expense and HST Tracker T2125 (Sample).xlsx: filled in for a made up Toronto photographer, so you can see how it works.
• Start Here.pdf: a one page guide.

How to open it
• Excel 2016 or later: open the file. If a yellow Protected View bar shows at the top, click Enable Editing.
• Google Sheets: upload the file to Google Drive. Right click it, choose Open with, then Google Sheets. Then choose File, Save as Google Sheets, and work in that copy.
• Apple Numbers on a Mac: right click the file, choose Open With, then Numbers.
Type only in the pale green cells. Everything else fills in by itself. In Excel the other cells are locked with no password, so a formula can't be wiped by mistake. The locks may not carry over to Google Sheets and do not carry over to Numbers, so take extra care there.

What it does not do
It does not file your income tax or GST/HST return, connect to your bank or make invoices. PST and QST are not tracked. CCA is not worked out; if you claim it, type the amount on one Expenses row. If you are registered, type the GST/HST you can claim back on equipment on a CCA row and it counts as an input tax credit with either method (the CRA allows the full credit when you use the equipment more than 50% for business, and none at 50% or less, where the GST/HST becomes part of the cost you depreciate). It handles one vehicle and one GST/HST method for the whole year. GST/HST you pay on home office costs stays part of the expense and is not claimed as an input tax credit.

How it was made
AI tools help build and check the formulas in this file. Every rate, limit and deadline was checked against official CRA sources, and the Rates sheet shows the year and source for each one. The line numbers are from the 2025 Form T2125.

For record keeping and planning, not tax advice.

results.description:
For small business owners and freelancers: record money actually received or paid, then compare each recorded account balance with your month-end statement. An editable Excel workbook with a blank file, fictional worked example and step-by-step guide.

WHAT YOU RECEIVE
One ZIP containing BLANK.xlsx, DEMO.xlsx, START-HERE.html and RELEASE-NOTES.txt. Five workbook tabs: Overview, Accounts, Transactions, Balances and Guide. Up to 500 transaction rows, three accounts, twelve monthly reviews per account. One calendar year and one currency per file. English-language files.

HOW IT WORKS
1. Set year, currency label, account IDs and January 1 opening balances.
2. Record income, expenses, refunds, owner contributions/withdrawals and transfers. Yellow cells are inputs. Invalid and Void rows are excluded; input-status flags identify errors.
3. Select a month to review cash income and expenses. Owner funds and transfers affect balances without counting as operating income/expense.
4. Enter each statement closing balance manually. Recorded minus statement gives the difference to investigate. A matching balance does not prove records complete or classified correctly.
5. Review records and save a dated XLSX copy as a backup.

FICTIONAL EXAMPLE
Income 3,400 minus expenses 2,150 = recorded balance 1,250. Manually entered statement balance 1,230 = difference 20 to review.

COMPATIBILITY
Microsoft Excel desktop required and not included. Opening, editing, recalculation, saving and reopening tested in Windows desktop Excel. Google Sheets, Excel web, Mac and mobile are not verified. No macros. Formulas are not locked: edit yellow inputs only; do not insert rows or exceed capacity. Use ordinary cent precision and dates without time. Currency is a label, not conversion.

SAVE & BACKUP
Save dated XLSX copies separately. Restore by opening a saved copy and checking accounts, year and records. CSV/PDF are not workbook backups.

CHOOSE THE RIGHT MAXORI TOOL
This workbook records actual cash transactions and compares account balances. Cash & Invoice Desk manages documents and collections; Bills & Renewals tracks future payment dates. Data must be transferred manually; no automatic sync between these tools. Avoid counting the same payment twice.

LIMITS & LICENSE
Operational cash tracking, not certified accounting or tax filing. No bank import, accruals, payroll, tax computation, depreciation or receipt completeness detection. results.title: Small Business Bookkeeping Spreadsheet | Google Sheets + Excel Income Expense Tracker, P&L, Schedule C, Bank Reconciliation
results.description:
Bookkeeping that actually balances.

Stop guessing whether you made money this month. Enter each sale or expense on one line, and this spreadsheet does the rest: a live dashboard, a month-by-month profit and loss, a monthly check against your bank statement, and a Schedule C worksheet with your totals already on the right lines when tax time comes.

Made for sole proprietors, freelancers, Etsy sellers, consultants, and anyone with a side hustle who wants clean books without learning accounting software.

WHAT YOU GET
• Google Sheets template (recommended) plus an Excel version of the same file
• Two looks in one purchase: a Dark theme and a Sage & Beige theme
• 8 tabs: Dashboard, Quick Start, Transactions, Monthly P&L, Reconcile, Schedule C, Settings, Categories
• 1,000 transaction rows
• A bank reconciliation tab that tells you each month whether your books match your statement
• Schedule C worksheet covering lines 1–7, 8–28, 30 and 31 plus Part III cost of goods sold
• Works on desktop, tablet, and phone through the Google Sheets app

THE DASHBOARD
Six headline numbers at a glance: income, expenses, net profit, how much to set aside for taxes, what you've paid yourself, and your estimated cash position. Below them, your top expenses, income vs expenses by month, and a net profit trend line. A loss shows in red. No formulas to touch.

THE TRANSACTIONS TAB
Date, description, who you paid or who paid you, a category dropdown, and the amount. That's it. The sheet works out the month, year, and whether it's income or an expense. Rows missing a date or category turn orange so nothing slips through. Rows from another tax year are greyed out and left out of the totals.

MONTHLY P&L
Every category by month with year-to-date totals, net profit, and net margin. Owner draws and personal spending are tracked separately, so they lower your cash but never distort your profit. Most free templates get this wrong.

RECONCILIATION
Once a month, type the ending balance from your bank statement. The Reconcile tab works out what your books say you should have (starting cash plus everything you logged, owner draws included) and shows Balanced or exactly how far off you are, month by month. It also counts transactions that have no category yet, since those are the usual reason a month won't balance.

SCHEDULE C WORKSHEET
A worksheet to review with your tax preparer, laid out like the form: gross receipts, returns and allowances (line 2), cost of goods sold (line 4, from a Part III section with beginning and ending inventory), gross profit, every expense line from 8 to 27a, total expenses, the home office deduction on line 30 using the IRS simplified method ($5 per square foot, up to 300 square feet), and net profit on line 31. Other expenses on line 27a are listed category by category, and the 50% meals rule is already applied. Every category, including the ones you add, carries its own Schedule C line, so nothing gets lost.

SETTINGS YOU CONTROL
Business name, tax year, tax set-aside percentage, meals deductible percentage, starting cash balance, inventory at the start and end of the year, and home office square footage. Rename any category, or add up to 30 of your own and pick the Schedule C line for each; they appear in the dropdown and are counted in the P&L and the worksheet.

HOW IT WORKS
1. Download the PDF with your access link after purchase.
2. Click the link and choose "Make a copy" to save it to your Google Drive.
3. Follow the 5-step Quick Start tab. You'll be entering transactions in under five minutes.
Prefer Excel? The .xlsx files are included in the same download.

PLEASE NOTE
• This is a digital download. No physical item will be shipped.
• You need a free Google account for the Google Sheets version, or Excel 2016 or later for the Excel version.
• One tax year per file. Make a new copy each January.
• Inventory is a simple start-of-year and end-of-year count you enter yourself; there is no item-by-item inventory tracking.
• The home office line uses the simplified method only. If you use actual expenses (Form 8829), work that out with your preparer.
• This spreadsheet organizes your records. It is not tax advice. Confirm deductibility and filing positions with a tax professional.
• Using the Excel file? Clear rows by selecting just the input cells and pressing Delete. Don't insert, delete or sort whole rows; the calculated columns are locked.
• Because this is a digital product, refunds aren't offered. If something isn't working, message me and I'll fix it.

QUESTIONS?
Message me anytime. I work in accounting and built this because the templates I found online didn't add up. Every formula in this one has been tested against real numbers.

results.title: Bookkeeping Spreadsheet for Excel and Google Sheets, Small Business Accounts with Invoices and Bills
results.description:
A bookkeeping spreadsheet for Excel and Google Sheets. Record your invoices, your bills and your bank, and get a profit and loss, a balance sheet and a cash position out of them. 22 tabs, built for sole traders and small businesses.


⚠️ READ THIS BIT BEFORE YOU BUY

This is a single entry book. You record each payment once, the way it appears on your bank statement, and the reports are built from that.

It is not double entry and it is not accounting software. The practical difference is on the balance sheet: it does not prove itself. Some lines are worked out from what you have entered and some you type in yourself, and every line says which. A check at the foot of that tab tells you whether the two sides agree and by how much.

If you were looking for software that posts both sides of every entry, this is not that, and I would rather tell you now than take your money.


⚡ WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT

📒 Invoices and bills kept separate from the bank, because issuing an invoice and being paid for it are two different events
🏦 A proper bank reconciliation, with a per account difference against your statement
📊 A real profit and loss, built from invoices and bills rather than from what the bank happened to do
⚖️ A balance sheet that tells you the truth, including when it does not agree
✅ 21 data checks before you send a figure to anyone


🔍 THE ONE THING THAT STOPS DOUBLE COUNTING

Every payment has a Reference column. If it holds a bill number, the expense is already counted from the bills tab, so the payment is not counted again. If it is blank, the payment is treated as a cost in its own right.

That single rule is what keeps the profit and loss honest. Most spreadsheets either count everything twice or make you keep two separate sets of figures.


📦 WHAT IS INSIDE: 22 TABS

1️⃣ SETUP 👉 Your business, year, tax system and bank accounts with opening balances

🏦 RECONCILE

results.title: Small Product Business System, Bookkeeping Spreadsheet Google Sheets & Excel, Inventory Tracker, Order Tracker, Pricing, Profit and Loss

Your shop's numbers in one place. Sales in one spot, receipts in another, stock counts in a notebook and prices worked out on a napkin? The Small Product Business System brings your income, expenses, inventory, orders and pricing into one spreadsheet for Google Sheets and Microsoft Excel. It's made for small product businesses, like handmade and digital shops that sell online or in person. White cells are for your numbers. Gray cells calculate on their own.

INSTANT DOWNLOAD. A spreadsheet file (.xlsx), not a printable PDF, not an app and not accounting software. No macros, no scripts, no add-ons. No subscription.

WHAT YOU GET
One ZIP file (Small-Product-Business-System.zip) with:
- the workbook: 12 connected tabs
- a SAMPLE file filled in with a fictional example shop, so you can see every tab working
- a 5-page PDF guide

WHAT'S INSIDE: 12 TABS
1. Start Here: 5 setup steps, links to every tab, how the cells work and a few things worth knowing.

2. Dashboard: the year at a glance: total income, total costs, net profit and margin, orders, units sold and stock alerts. Charts show income and net profit by month, sales by channel and your top 5 products, plus quick numbers like gross margin, fees as a % of sales, best month, stock value and orders to ship.

3. Settings: business name, currency symbol (before or after the amount), the year to report, your hourly rate, your target margin and a mileage rate. Below that: up to 8 sales channels with the fee rates you enter, and every dropdown list. 5 channels, 6 product categories and 15 expense categories are ready to use, and you can rename them.

4. Products & Pricing: up to 100 products. Enter materials, packaging and other costs per item, minutes to make one and your price. It shows labor cost, product cost, full cost, estimated fees, profit per item, margin, the price you'd need for your target margin, and a Check flag (for example LOSS when the price is below cost).

5. Fee Estimator: try one order (pick a product or type a price, quantity and shipping) and compare every channel side by side: fees, shipping, product cost, what you keep and your margin.

6. Inventory: stock for every product, with starting stock, what you make or restock and adjustments. Sold comes from Orders. Status shows OK, Low: restock, Out of stock or Oversold. On the right: a materials and supplies list (50 rows) with reorder levels.

7. Orders: one row per product per order, 500 rows. Pick the channel and product, and the price, product cost, estimated fees and profit fill in. Optional: price override, discount, shipping charged, actual fees (used instead of the estimate), your shipping cost, status and notes.

8. Income: up to 200 rows of income that isn't an order (workshops, commissions...), plus sales by channel for the year.

9. Expenses: every business expense, one per row (500 rows), with a yearly summary by category.

10. Mileage: an optional log of business trips (200 rows), valued at the rate you choose. You decide whether it counts in the P&L.

11. Monthly P&L: profit and loss for each month and the year: sales, shipping charged, other income, fees, shipping you paid, cost of goods, gross profit, each expense category, net profit and net margin.

12. Annual Summary: the year on one page: totals, best month, quarters, sales channels and product categories.

WHY YOU MIGHT LIKE IT
- One file instead of several: bookkeeping, inventory, orders and pricing in the same spreadsheet.
- Pricing from your real costs: materials, packaging, other costs and your time go into each product's price and margin.
- Your fees, your numbers: you enter the fee rates for each sales channel yourself, so you can update them whenever a platform changes its pricing.
- Orders do the math: pick a product and the price, cost, fees and profit fill in, and stock goes down.
- Nothing is locked: rename categories, channels and lists in Settings.
- One-time purchase. The files are yours to keep.

HOW IT OPENS
- Works in Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets. Classic formulas only.
- Google Sheets: upload the .xlsx file to Google Drive, right-click it and choose Open with > Google Sheets, then File > Save as Google Sheets. Or open a blank Google Sheet and use File > Import > Upload.
- Charts can look slightly different in Google Sheets than in Excel.
- Phone or tablet: fine for viewing. Set it up and enter data on a computer. Nothing is locked.
- You need Microsoft Excel or a Google account.

HOW DELIVERY WORKS
1. After your payment is confirmed, go to Your account > Purchases, find this order and choose Download Files. You'll also get an email with a download link (check your spam folder if you can't find it). Use a web browser rather than the mobile app to download.
2. Unzip Small-Product-Business-System.zip. Inside: Small-Product-Business-System.xlsx (your blank workbook), Small-Product-Business-System-SAMPLE.xlsx and Small-Product-Business-System-How-to-Use.pdf.
3. Open the workbook in Microsoft Excel (if you see Protected View, click Enable Editing), or open it in Google Sheets as described above.
4. Follow the 5 steps on the Start Here tab.
Nothing is shipped. This is a digital download only.

IMPORTANT: NOT TAX OR FINANCIAL ADVICE
This spreadsheet is a record-keeping and planning tool. It isn't tax, accounting or financial advice, and it can't promise any income or profit. Prices, fees, margins and profit figures are estimates based on the numbers you enter. The fee rates in the file are examples, not any platform's real fees: check your platform's current fee page and type in your own. For tax questions, talk to a qualified accountant or tax advisor where you live.

FAQ
Which sales channels does it work with?
Any you sell on. Settings has up to 8 channels (5 are filled in, like your own website, markets and fairs, wholesale and an online marketplace). Rename them and type in each channel's fee rates: a percentage of the order, a fixed fee per order, payment processing, a listing fee per item and an ads percentage.

Does it calculate my taxes?
No. It helps you keep your income, expenses and profit and loss organized, but it doesn't calculate tax or give tax advice. Check your local rules or ask an accountant.

Can it import my sales reports automatically?
No. You enter orders yourself, one row per product per order, and the rest fills in.

Which currency can I use?
Pick a currency symbol from the list in Settings or type your own, and choose whether it shows before or after the amount.

Can I change the categories?
Yes. 6 product categories and 15 expense categories are ready to use, and you can rename them or add your own in Settings (up to 12 product categories and 18 expense categories). Each expense category is marked as a product cost or an operating expense.

Does it count my time?
Your hourly rate is used for pricing (full cost and suggested price). The P&L counts product cost without labor, so net profit is what's left to pay yourself.

What's the SAMPLE file?
A copy filled in with a fictional example shop, so you can see every tab in action. Use the blank file for your own business.

This spreadsheet system was designed by Tulle & Tally Studio with the help of AI tools. The spreadsheet's layout, formulas, wording, sample data and PDF guide were written with AI assistance. The listing photos are renders of the actual spreadsheet file, assembled by script; they are not AI-generated pictures. The shop in the sample file is fictional.

results.description:
Etsy shows you your gross sales. It does not show you what you actually earned. After listing fees, transaction fees, payment processing, advertising costs, cost of goods sold and the tax you owe on the profit — the number that ends up in your bank account can be significantly smaller than the number Etsy shows on your dashboard.

The Etsy Seller Finance Tracker fills that gap. Seven tabs that go from raw sales data through to annual P&L, with a fee calculator that shows exactly what Etsy takes from every single sale, and a product profitability tab that ranks your products by actual margin — not by revenue.

✦ THE THREE NUMBERS EVERY ETSY SELLER NEEDS TO KNOW

Gross Revenue is what Etsy shows you. Net Revenue is what you receive after fees. Profit is what you keep after your costs. Most Etsy sellers know the first number well. Many are vague on the second. Almost none have calculated the third for every individual product in their shop.

The Product Profitability tab changes that. Enter your material cost, time cost and any platform-specific costs for each product. The tab ranks every item by net margin. Some products you thought were popular turn out to barely cover costs. Some products you've been underpricing have margins you didn't know you had.

📋 Sales Tracker — log every sale with date, product, quantity, price, platform fees and net received. SUMIF formulas aggregate automatically into the dashboard
💰 Fee Calculator — enter any sale price and the calculator shows Etsy's listing fee, transaction fee and payment processing fee — and your net payout — instantly. Run scenarios before pricing
🏷 Product Profitability — all products ranked by net margin after fees and COGS. Identifies your most and least profitable products. Highlights any product selling at a loss

results.title: Alles-In-Eén Financiën Spreadsheet Bundel voor Google Sheets
results.description:
Een alles-in-één pakket voor persoonlijke financiën in Google Spreadsheets. Alles wat je nodig hebt om je financiën bij te houden en te verbeteren. Het spreadsheetpakket bevat een schulden tracker, een budget spreadsheet, een spaar tracker en een spreadsheet voor je vermogen.

Alle spreadsheets zijn zo gemaakt dat ze extreem gebruiksvriendelijk zijn. Je hebt zelfs geen ervaring met Google Sheets nodig. En hoewel ze minimalistisch zijn in ontwerp, zijn de finance trackers tegelijkertijd allesomvattend. Dus of je nu een beginner bent of een doorgewinterde goeroe, deze set van spreadsheets biedt je alles wat je nodig hebt.

Lees hieronder verder voor meer informatie over elke spreadsheet. Proost op het verbeteren van je persoonlijke financiën. Je kunt het!

SCHULDEN TRACKER
- Vergelijk en kies de strategie van je keuze: de sneeuwbalmethode, de lawinemethode of een aangepaste volgorde voor het afbetalen van je schulden.
- Volg tot 30 schulden tot 30 jaar.
- Pas je betalingen op elk gewenst moment aan.
- Je vindt alles wat je nodig hebt op één sheet. Je hoeft niet te schakelen tussen verschillende bladen, tabbladen of weergaven. Van overzichten en aflossingsdata tot exacte betalingen: alles staat op één pagina.
- Er zijn slechts vier stappen om aan de slag te gaan: stel je startdatum in, kies een strategie (sneeuwbal/lawine/aangepast), selecteer je eerste extra maandelijkse betaling en voeg de basisgegevens van elke schuld toe. De spreadsheet berekent vervolgens automatisch al je betalingen en aflossingsdata per schuld.

BUDGET SPREADSHEET
- De budget tracker werkt voor elke periode: maandelijks, wekelijks, tweewekelijks, per salarisbetaling of een ander gewenst tijdsbestek.
- Je kunt je budget binnen enkele minuten opzetten. Stapsgewijze instructies worden meegeleverd, evenals een voorbeeldwerkblad. Dankzij de vele automatische berekeningen wordt het zware werk voor jou in plaats van door jou gedaan.
- Alles wat je nodig hebt, staat op één werkblad. Bovenaan vind je overzichten, grafieken en details per categorie en subcategorie. Daaronder is plek voor al je transacties, die automatisch de rest van het werkblad invullen. Een overzicht van je uitgaven laat zien waar je geld naartoe gaat.

SPAARTRACKER
- Je kunt tot 20 fondsen / spaarpotjes toevoegen aan de spaarfondstracker.
- Om te beginnen voer je eenvoudig de basisgegevens in in slechts 3 cellen, en je ziet je grafieken tot leven komen! 
- Uniek aan deze spreadsheet is dat alles op één blad staat in plaats van op meerdere tabbladen. Met een overzicht per fonds bovenaan en stortingen/opnames eronder, heb je alles op één plek.

NETTO VERMOGENSTRACKER
- Bereken je huidige netto vermogen en zie hoe het zich in de loop der tijd ontwikkelt.
- Vier stappen om de tracker in te stellen:
Stap 1: Stel je startdatum in.
Stap 2: Pas indien nodig categorieën aan.
Stap 3: Voeg je huidige activa en passiva toe.
Stap 4: Werk je cijfers maandelijks bij.
- Alles staat handig op één tabblad. Op dit blad vind je totalen, grafieken, activa en passiva. Je kunt een paar maanden, een jaar of meerdere jaren bijhouden.

results.description:
Creating a budget for couples is an important step in managing shared finances and achieving financial goals together. Here are some key considerations and steps to follow when setting up a budget:

Open Communication: Start by having open and honest conversations with your partner about your financial goals, priorities, and any concerns or limitations you may have. This lays the foundation for effective budgeting as a couple.

Combine Income and Expenses: Gather information about both partners' income sources and determine the total monthly income available for budgeting. Similarly, compile a list of all shared expenses, such as rent/mortgage, utilities, groceries, transportation, and debt payments.

Allocate Funds: Discuss and agree upon how to allocate the available income towards different categories. This includes determining the percentage or specific amounts to be allocated for essential expenses, savings, debt repayment, and discretionary spending.

Prioritize Savings: Set aside a portion of your budget for savings, including emergency funds, retirement contributions, and other financial goals you may have as a couple. Aim to save a specific percentage of your income each month.

Track and Monitor: Use budgeting tools or apps to track your expenses and income regularly. This helps you stay aware of your financial progress and make adjustments as needed. Review your budget together periodically and make any necessary modifications.

Flexibility and Compromise: Recognize that financial situations can change, and it's important to be flexible and willing to compromise. Adjust the budget as circumstances evolve, and always be open to discussing financial decisions together.

Regular Communication: Maintain ongoing communication about financial matters, including any changes in income, expenses, or financial goals. This ensures that both partners are informed and involved in the budgeting process.

Remember, creating a budget as a couple is a collaborative effort that requires trust, transparency, and shared commitment to financial well-being. By working together, you can effectively manage your finances and achieve your joint financial goals.

results.title: Budget couple 2027 au prorata des revenus, tableur budget familial dépenses communes, Excel Google Sheets français

Qui paie quoi, et qui doit combien ? Entre le loyer payé par l'un, les courses par l'autre et la facture d'électricité, les comptes deviennent vite flous. Ce tableur répartit vos dépenses communes selon vos revenus et vous l'écrit en clair chaque mois, par exemple : « Thomas doit 352,55 € à Julie ».

Pourquoi au prorata ? Parce que partager à 50/50 n'est pas toujours juste quand l'un gagne plus que l'autre. Avec 2 400 € et 1 600 € de revenus, l'un paie 60 % des dépenses communes et l'autre 40 % : chacun participe selon ses moyens. Vous préférez le 50/50 ou un pourcentage à vous, comme 55/45 ? Il suffit de le choisir dans une liste.

Au quotidien, c'est simple :
• vous indiquez vos prénoms, vos revenus nets et votre façon de partager ;
• vous notez chaque dépense et qui l'a payée ;
• l'un a avancé une dépense personnelle pour l'autre ? Vous l'indiquez : elle lui est due en entier, le reste est partagé ;
• vous choisissez le mois, et le tableur affiche la part de chacun, ce qui a été payé et le solde.

Vous avez un compte joint ? L'onglet « Compte commun » calcule combien chacun doit y virer chaque mois pour couvrir le loyer, l'énergie, les courses…, toujours au prorata. Si un revenu change en cours d'année (une prime, un temps partiel), vous corrigez le mois concerné et le calcul suit. Le bilan annuel cumule les soldes mois après mois.

Pas besoin d'attendre janvier : l'année se change en une case dans les « Paramètres ». Vous pouvez commencer dès maintenant sur 2026, puis repartir d'une nouvelle copie pour 2027.

results.description:
When one of you earns more, should that person pay more? With two incomes in one household, money can turn into a running argument about who paid for what.

See it set up
Want to see it in action first? Here's a step-by-step video of the whole setup, filmed in real Excel: https://youtu.be/d83WrIjo1q8 (Etsy won't let me make outside links clickable, so you'll need to copy it into your browser.)

This budget helps settle it fairly. You can split shared costs by income (whoever earns more puts in more), 50/50 or by a share you choose, and it works out what each of you puts into the joint account each month. Log every purchase once, with who paid and whose it was, and at the end of the month it tells you plainly who owes whom, down to the cent.

What's inside — 6 connected tabs

Dashboard
The month at a glance: your take-home together, the shared budget and your own budgets, what you've spent, what's left and the settle-up. Then each of you side by side: your share, what you put in, your own spending and what you paid toward shared costs.

Setup
Your names, how you'd like to split and the month to show.

Income
What each of you takes home each month.

Spending
Every purchase, who paid (either of you or the joint account) and whose it was: shared, or one of yours.

Budget
The shared costs and each of your own budgets, next to this month's spending.

Goals
What you're saving for together, and what it takes each month to get there on time.

The sample's couple
In the sample, Alex and Jordan split shared costs by income. Alex's share is 54%, so Alex puts $1,838.20 a month into the joint account and Jordan puts in $1,571.80. Rent and the internet come out of the joint account, and one of them paid for the rest of September's shared costs personally. At the end of the month, Alex owes Jordan $5.81.

Goes well with
The Paycheck Budget Planner, to plan each of your paychecks.

What you get
An instant download: one Excel file (.xlsx), a setup guide (PDF) and the how-to video (MP4). There are no macros, nothing to install and no subscription. The formulas are locked so you can't overwrite one by accident, and the sheet password is printed in the guide. It's your file, after all.
Save a copy each month, after you settle up.

Questions or problems?
Just send me a message through Etsy and I'll get back to you within 2 business days. If something isn't working the way you expected, let me know which tab and cell you're on. It usually only takes one message to sort out, and I'd much rather help than have you struggle with it.

What it runs on

Excel 2016 or newer, on Windows or Mac (Microsoft 365 included), and Google Sheets.

It doesn't lean on any of the newer features that only Excel 2021 and Microsoft 365 have, so an older copy of Excel runs it just fine.

Google Sheets has every function it uses. The one thing that doesn't carry over is Excel's formula lock, so take care not to type over a formula there.

SPLIT THE BILLS. KNOW WHO OWES WHAT. 🌿

COUPLES BUDGET is a budget spreadsheet and shared expense tracker that calculates each partner’s share and what is left to pay back.

💡 YOUR AGREEMENT DOESN’T HAVE TO BE 50/50

Choose how to split shared expenses:
• Equally.
• In proportion to your incomes.
• Using your own custom percentage.

For example: Alex pays $1,000 in rent. With a 60/40 split, Alex’s share is $600 and Sam’s is $400. The workbook shows that Sam owes Alex $400. Once you record that repayment, the remaining settlement balance is zero.

✨ WHAT YOU CAN TRACK

• Shared and personal purchases, including who paid.
• Each partner’s share of shared expenses.
• Who owes whom and the remaining amount to settle.
• Store refunds and payments between partners.
• Upcoming bills and unpaid amounts.
• Your remaining shared budget.
• Shared savings deposits and withdrawals.
• Progress toward one savings goal.
• Incomplete entries and transactions outside your selected period.

📦 WHAT YOU RECEIVE

One ZIP file containing:
• 1 desktop .xlsx workbook with a dashboard and two automatic charts.
• 1 mobile and tablet .xlsx workbook with vertical entry cards.
• 1 illustrated 6-page PDF guide with instructions and a worked example.

English edition with USD amounts and MM/DD/YYYY dates.

Each layout is supplied as one .xlsx file to open or import in your chosen spreadsheet app.

📝 HOW TO START

1. Choose the desktop or mobile layout and save a working copy.
2. Enter your names, date range and preferred split.
3. Log expenses and who paid.
4. Record money paid back between partners.
5. Check your overview, upcoming bills and shared savings.

Cream cells: your entries.
Green cells: automatic calculations.

📱 DESKTOP, MOBILE AND TABLET

The desktop layout uses row-based tables and charts. The mobile layout organizes entries into vertical cards with larger input areas.

These are two independent alternatives. They do not sync with each other. Choose one working copy. To enter data together, share that same copy through your spreadsheet app.

💻 OPENING AND COMPATIBILITY

.xlsx format with no macros, VBA or add-ins.

• Microsoft Excel: open the workbook.
• Google Sheets: upload to Drive and open or convert with Google Sheets.
• Apple Numbers: import the workbook on Mac, iPhone or iPad.

Appearance, charts, dropdowns and navigation buttons may vary after import. The guide includes opening instructions and alternative ways to navigate and enter data.

Calculations were checked through test cases and recalculation in LibreOffice. Direct testing in Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets or Apple Numbers has not been performed.

• 300 expenses.
• 100 settlements.
• 60 upcoming bills.
• 100 savings entries.
• 12 editable categories.
